purpose: How a commercial cleaning broker builds and holds the delivery side of the business: mapping and vetting the crews and subcontracted cleaning companies that can actually hold a building, choosing an engagement structure with the classification-risk factors verified by a qualified professional rather than assumed, handing the sold scope over so the crew delivers exactly what was bid, turning the word clean into an inspectable standard with a risk-weighted walkthrough cadence and a scoring instrument that produces evidence, deciding who owns supplies and equipment, and arranging coverage and replacement before a crew fails rather than after.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the delivery unit is one site-shift at one contracted building performed by a crew the broker arranged, and the broker keeps only what is left of the client's monthly price after the crew, consumables, inspection time, coverage, remedy and administration are paid, so every sourcing and quality decision here is judged by whether the site can be delivered to standard at a cost the signed price can carry for the whole term

no crew price, hourly pay, cleaning-hours-per-visit figure, consumable cost, coverage premium, spread percentage or roster size in this knowledge base is a market rate or an industry benchmark; each is a MECHANISM the broker measures inside its own quotes, walkthroughs, inspection records and delivered costs and re-measures for every site and every crew

worker classification, coverage and bonding obligations, background-check duties, facility-specific compliance rules and the enforceability of any crew agreement term are named only as obligation CLASSES; each varies by jurisdiction, facility type, client contract and year, must be verified with a qualified professional and the current authority before anything is committed, and is never carried across from a prior crew, a prior contract or another jurisdiction by assumption

the client was told before signing that cleaning is performed by contracted crews the broker sources, supervises and stands behind, and every delivery-side artifact, introduction, badge, uniform and coverage visit must stay consistent with that statement

crews are small businesses of widely varying commercial sophistication, capitalisation and command of the contract language, so the duty to explain terms plainly and to deal fairly scales with that gap in exactly the way it does with an unsophisticated buyer on the acquisition side

margin is created at bid time and either preserved or consumed here: a scope handed over incompletely, a crew priced below what the task list physically takes, or an inspection regime that produces no evidence all show up later as cost the signed price cannot absorb
this knowledge base is educational business-process knowledge; it is not personalised legal, tax, employment, insurance or financial advice for any particular broker, crew, contract or jurisdiction
exclusions: choosing which facility classes to pursue, reading a buyer's purchasing process, the sales walkthrough that produces the measured scope, the labour-load and cost build that sets the bid, proposal construction, client-facing contract terms and honest differentiation in the sale: owned by the contract acquisition and bid strategy knowledge base, which hands this one a signed scope rather than receiving one from it

month-to-month margin health of a live contract, crew cost drift and scope creep read as margin mechanisms, the client complaint-response system as a retention engine, renewal and repricing conversations, account expansion into added frequency, add-on services and sister sites, and the decision to exit an unprofitable contract: owned by the margin management, client retention and renewals knowledge base, which this one feeds with inspection evidence and delivered-cost facts

any statement of what a crew is paid, what a site costs to clean, how many cleaning hours a building takes, what a coverage call costs or what a broker's spread should be, presented as a figure of fact rather than as a mechanism the broker measures in its own quotes and records

legal conclusions about worker classification, joint employment, coverage adequacy, bonding, agreement enforceability, non-solicitation scope or facility compliance duties for any particular crew, arrangement or jurisdiction; these are named as obligation classes, flagged for verification by a qualified professional in the jurisdiction of performance, and never resolved here

any practice that misrepresents who performs the cleaning: uniforms, badges, sign-in entries, email signatures or silences that imply the crew are the broker's employees when they are not, concealing a missed shift or a coverage substitution from the client, or telling a crew to present itself as something the client was never told

coercive dealing with crews: invented competing quotes used to force a price down, threats to withdraw other sites as negotiating leverage, retroactive deductions the crew was never shown, and any use of a crew principal's dependence, language, inexperience or immigration status to extract terms they do not understand

instructing anyone how to clean: chemical selection, dilution, equipment operation, floor-care and carpet technique, and infection-control procedure are the crew's professional domain, and this knowledge base specifies observable outcomes and site rules rather than method

payroll administration, benefits programmes and employment-law compliance systems for a broker that chooses an employee model, which are named here as an obligation class to resolve with a qualified professional and a payroll provider rather than built inside this knowledge base

residential and household cleaning crews, one-off consumer jobs and franchise-system purchase decisions, which have different labour supply, economics and obligation classes than the commercial contracts this delivery method serves

competency_questions.question: A contract is signed - what exactly do I now owe the client on the delivery side, and what has to come out of the money before any of it is mine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DELIVERY_MANDATE_FRAME states the site-shift as the delivery unit, the bought task list and visit pattern, the costed labour load the price was built on and every cost class the residual must still absorb, and CREW_PRICING_AND_QUOTE_MECHANISM shows the crew price tested against that load rather than against other quotes alone

competency_questions.question: What kind of relationship should I have with the people who clean, and what must be professionally verified before I commit to that structure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLASSIFICATION_RISK_STRUCTURE enumerates the factor classes a classification analysis weighs, maps the broker's intended operating pattern onto them and requires written verification with a qualified professional in the jurisdiction of performance before commitment, and ENGAGEMENT_AGREEMENT_TERMS shows the agreement language matching the operating pattern rather than contradicting it

competency_questions.question: What does the client have to be told about who is actually in their building, and how do I keep the crew's arrival consistent with what was sold?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_DISCLOSURE_CONSISTENCY gives the asymmetric rule that accountability may be promised but employment may never be implied, and CREW_ONBOARDING_WALKTHROUGH shows the introduction moment where the client meets the crew as the contracted crew the broker arranged

competency_questions.question: Which coverage and bonding obligation classes must a crew hold before it touches a site, and how do I stop them lapsing quietly mid-term?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_INSURANCE_AND_BONDING_VERIFICATION names the obligation classes, the verification method that avoids forwarded documents and mismatched named insureds, and the expiry-with-suspension rule, and CREW_PERFORMANCE_RECORD_AND_HANDOFF holds the certificate dates as a tracked field with an owner

competency_questions.question: What am I not allowed to do to a crew to get a better price, and why does doing it cost me anyway?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_SIDE_ETHICS_AND_FAIR_DEALING names disclosure-first sourcing, the forbidden leverage tactics and the raised duty where a principal's understanding is limited, and CREW_PRICING_AND_QUOTE_MECHANISM shows why a crew squeezed below sustainability returns as deficiencies, coverage cost and client risk

competency_questions.question: Where do I find crews before I need one, and how do I keep a bench that is actually warm rather than a list of names?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_SUPPLY_MAP enumerates the supply classes, the channels that find them and the fields kept per crew including route geography and capacity headroom with contact recency, and CREW_PORTFOLIO_AND_CONCENTRATION shows the coverage and concentration exposures the bench is maintained against

competency_questions.question: How do I tell a crew that can hold this specific building from one that will fail on it, before I have committed anything?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_QUALIFICATION_SCREEN states the site-specific screening questions and the recorded fit or no-fit decision, and CREW_REFERENCE_AND_SITE_VERIFICATION shows the specific reference questions, the visit to a site the crew already cleans and the entity check that catches onward subcontracting

competency_questions.question: What has to be in the crew lead's hands on the first night so the building gets exactly what the proposal promised?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_HANDOFF_PACK lists the room-by-room task cards, frequency calendar, marked plan, special instructions, exclusions, supply location and escalation rule with versioning, and CREW_ONBOARDING_WALKTHROUGH shows the joint walkthrough that calibrates the standard before the first billed shift

competency_questions.question: How do keys, codes and after-hours access stay controlled across a crew change without turning into a security incident?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_ACCESS_AND_KEY_CONTROL describes the issuance register, individual codes, facility access rules and the rule that an unaccounted credential forces a rekey or code change with client notification, and CREW_FAILURE_DIAGNOSIS_AND_TRANSITION places the credential audit in the replacement sequence before the incoming crew is issued anything

competency_questions.question: How often should I walk which sites, and what makes an inspection score mean something instead of being a number I made up?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALITY_STANDARD_DEFINITION states observable per-task standards and tolerances, INSPECTION_CADENCE_DESIGN allocates frequency by consequence with reset rules and varied hours, and QUALITY_SCORING_SYSTEM supplies the weighted instrument, the dated-photograph evidence rule and the inspector calibration guard

competency_questions.question: An inspection fails - what happens next, in what order, and at what point does correcting become replacing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFICIENCY_REMEDY_LOOP gives the documented notice, sized correction window, re-inspection and written escalation ladder with remedies applied prospectively and explained beforehand, and CREW_FAILURE_DIAGNOSIS_AND_TRANSITION gives the cause diagnosis that decides between changing the condition, coaching and replacing

competency_questions.question: Who buys the paper towels, who owns the auto-scrubber, and what does that choice do to my cost and to the classification question?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLIES_AND_EQUIPMENT_MODEL sets out the responsibility patterns with their differing cost behaviour, restock triggers and equipment disposition on crew change, and CLASSIFICATION_RISK_STRUCTURE names equipment provision as one of the factor classes a classification analysis weighs

competency_questions.question: A crew does not show up on a Friday night - what is already in place, and what do I tell the client?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BACKUP_COVERAGE_SYSTEM describes detection, the pre-briefed named alternate, an access path independent of the absent crew and the truthful client communication rule, and CREW_DISCLOSURE_CONSISTENCY forbids presenting a coverage crew as anything other than what it is

competency_questions.question: What does the crew and site record have to contain so that the next building assignment, a crew price increase and the renewal decision are made on evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_PERFORMANCE_RECORD_AND_HANDOFF enumerates the per-crew and per-site fields, names the three downstream decisions it serves and states the transition gate, and QUALITY_SCORING_SYSTEM supplies the scored evidence trail the record carries

glossary.definition: The number of crew-hours per visit the signed price was built to absorb at a given site; the delivery-side yardstick every crew quote and staffing plan is tested against, measured from the broker's own bid rather than taken from any published rate.

One crew visit to one contracted building on one date; the unit in which delivery succeeds or fails, because missed nights, deficiencies, access problems and coverage costs all attach to a specific visit rather than to a month.

The chosen legal and commercial form of the relationship with the people who clean - broker employees, an independent cleaning company with its own crew and clients, a staffing or professional-employer arrangement, or a hybrid - selected only after the classification factor classes are mapped and verified with a qualified professional for the jurisdiction of performance.

The categories of evidence that worker-classification tests commonly weigh - direction of manner and method, schedule control, provision of equipment and consumables, whether the worker holds and markets to other clients, integration into the hiring party's core service, the written agreement, the payment basis, and duration and exclusivity - used here as a decision mechanism, never as a legal conclusion.

glossary.term: certificate of insurance and additional-insured endorsement
glossary.definition: The evidence document a crew's insurer or agent issues showing the coverage classes, named insured and policy dates, and the separate endorsement that extends specified rights to another party where a client contract requires it; verified with the issuing agent, matched to the signing entity, and tracked to expiry rather than filed and forgotten.

The obligation class covering client property and cash exposure arising from the people who hold keys and work unsupervised after hours; whether it is required, in what form and at what limit is a per-contract and per-jurisdiction question for a licensed insurance professional.

The versioned, site-specific document set that converts the bid's measured task list and frequency matrix into instructions a crew lead can work from unaided at night: room-by-room task cards, a dated frequency calendar, a marked plan, special instructions, stated exclusions, supply locations and escalation contacts.

A number produced by walking a site against the written standard, scoring area types weighted by client sensitivity and labour share, with every deficiency carrying a dated photograph; useful only as a trend across inspections and only when two inspectors on the same night would produce nearly the same figure.

The written record of a specific failed task with its date, photograph and the standard clause it missed, paired with a correction period sized to the deficiency and closed by a re-inspection against the same record; the rung of the ladder that precedes any contractual remedy.

A qualified, verified alternate crew that has already received the site's scope summary and agreed emergency terms and knows how it would gain access, maintained warm through recent contact so that coverage on a failed night is a call rather than a search.

nodes.definition: The moment a cleaning contract is signed the broker acquires a delivery obligation with a fixed price on one side and an open cost on the other, and this unit of work fixes exactly what that obligation is before any crew is approached. The mandate names the building, the task list and frequency the client actually bought, the visit pattern and hours the price was built on, and the costed labour load the bid assumed - the crew-hours per visit the signed price can absorb. It then names every cost class that must still be paid out of what is left after the crew: consumables the broker agreed to supply, equipment and its maintenance, the broker's own inspection time, coverage on nights a crew fails, remedy and rework, and administration and the broker's own coverage classes. The unit of account is the site-shift rather than the month, because everything that goes wrong goes wrong on a particular night in a particular building. Framed this way the mandate becomes the yardstick for every later decision: a crew quote is judged against the costed labour load, an inspection score against the bought task list, a coverage arrangement against the visit pattern. Nothing here re-opens the bid; if the mandate cannot be delivered at a crew price that is sustainable, that is a finding routed back to the acquisition side and forward to the margin side, not a problem to be solved by squeezing whoever cleans.

included: the bought task list, frequency and visit pattern restated as a delivery obligation
the costed labour load as the yardstick for crew quotes
the cost classes the residual must absorb after the crew is paid
the site-shift as the unit of delivery
excluded: building or re-opening the bid and its labour-load math
client-facing contract terms and proposal language
month-to-month margin tracking of the live account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the signed scope, frequency or access pattern changes, or delivered cost at the site diverges from the cost classes the mandate named

pros.claim: Restating the obligation before sourcing stops the broker from shopping a scope it has not itself understood
pros.example: a bid priced for four visits a week with monthly floor burnishing is quoted to crews as exactly that, so no crew prices three visits and no periodic work and appears cheapest

pros.claim: Naming every non-crew cost class up front prevents treating the whole difference between client price and crew price as profit
pros.example: an office contract where broker-supplied liners, quarterly extraction and two inspection visits a month were never counted until the site had run for a season

cons.claim: A mandate written from the bid inherits any error the bid made, and restating it can give a wrong labour load the authority of a decision
cons.example: a walkthrough that missed a second-floor kitchen produces a mandate every crew quotes against, so the shortfall is invisible until the crew is on site

cons.claim: The framing adds a step before any crew is contacted, which is unwelcome when a start date is close
cons.example: a contract signed on the twenty-eighth with service beginning on the first leaves little appetite for restating what was just sold

failure_modes: treating the client price minus the crew price as take-home and discovering the omitted cost classes months later
quoting crews from the proposal's marketing language rather than from the measured task list
letting a close start date replace the mandate with an informal verbal brief nobody can later point to
acceptance_tests: the mandate names the site, the task list, the frequency, the visit pattern and the costed labour load in the same terms the bid used
every cost class that must be paid out of the residual is listed by name, including inspection time and coverage
a discrepancy between the mandate and what the walkthrough recorded is raised as a bid finding rather than absorbed silently
revisit_triggers: the client changes frequency, adds an area or alters access hours
a crew reports site conditions materially different from what the mandate describes
delivered cost at the site diverges from the cost classes the mandate listed

nodes.definition: How the people who clean are engaged - as the broker's own employees, as an independent cleaning company holding its own crew and its own clients, through a staffing or professional-employer arrangement, or in some hybrid - is the highest-consequence structural decision on the delivery side, and it is a legal question that varies by jurisdiction, by the authority applying the test inside that jurisdiction, and over time. This unit of work treats it as a decision mechanism rather than an answer. It enumerates the factor classes that classification analyses commonly weigh - who directs the manner and method of the work, who controls the schedule, who supplies equipment and consumables, whether the party holds and markets to other clients, whether the work is integrated into the hiring party's core service, whether there is a written agreement and what it actually describes, how the relationship is paid, and how long and how exclusive it is - and it asks the broker to map its intended operating pattern onto those classes before choosing a structure. Nearly every other decision in this domain touches at least one factor: inspection cadence touches direction, a broker-owned auto-scrubber touches equipment, an exclusivity clause touches independence, a fixed nightly start time touches schedule control. The rule this node enforces is absolute: the classification conclusion is never assumed, never carried across from a prior deal or another state, and never inferred from what competitors appear to do; it is verified in writing with a qualified professional and the current authority for the jurisdiction of performance before the structure is committed, and re-verified whenever the operating pattern or the rules change. Misclassification exposure is not a quality problem that appears next week - it is a back-assessment, penalty and liability class that can surface years later, which is why it sits upstream of sourcing rather than beside it.

included: the factor classes a classification analysis commonly weighs, used as a decision mechanism
mapping the intended operating pattern onto those factor classes before choosing a structure
the mandatory professional-verification step and its written record
re-verification when the operating pattern or the rules change
excluded: any conclusion about how a specific arrangement would be classified in a specific jurisdiction
payroll administration, benefits and employment-compliance systems for an employee model
tax treatment or reporting advice for the broker or the crew

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the operating pattern, a move into a new jurisdiction, or a professional advising that the applicable test or its application has changed

pros.claim: Mapping the operating pattern onto factor classes surfaces contradictions while they are still cheap to change
pros.example: a broker planning to set a fixed nightly start time, provide all equipment and require exclusivity discovers the pattern before writing twelve crew agreements around it

pros.claim: A written verification record with a named professional and a date is what makes a later review answerable
pros.example: an operating-pattern memo, the questions asked and the professional's written response filed against the engagement structure and refreshed when the pattern changed

cons.claim: Professional verification costs money and time before a single site has been staffed, and the answer may be jurisdiction-specific enough to need repeating
cons.example: a broker expanding into a neighbouring state or county finding the analysis it paid for does not transfer

cons.claim: Designing away from control indicia can weaken the supervision a client contract expects, forcing a genuine trade rather than a clever fix
cons.example: a facility that wants the broker directing crew hours on site pushing the arrangement toward a pattern the chosen structure was built to avoid

failure_modes: assuming a paper-only independent-contractor label survives an operating pattern that behaves differently
copying an engagement structure from another broker, another state or an internet template without verification
changing the operating pattern - taking over scheduling, providing all equipment, demanding exclusivity - without re-verifying the structure
treating the question as settled once and never revisiting it as rules and the business change
acceptance_tests: the intended operating pattern is written down factor class by factor class before a structure is chosen
a dated written verification from a qualified professional for the jurisdiction of performance exists and is filed against the structure
no knowledge-base output states a classification conclusion; every one routes the question to professional verification
a documented re-verification trigger list exists and has been applied at least once when the pattern changed
revisit_triggers: the broker begins directing crew schedules, methods or personnel more closely than the structure assumed
equipment or consumable provision shifts from the crew to the broker
a crew becomes effectively exclusive to the broker or loses its other clients
the broker operates in a new jurisdiction or an authority changes the applicable test

nodes.definition: The client bought the service knowing that the cleaning is performed by contracted crews the broker sources, supervises and stands behind, and this unit of work keeps every delivery-side artifact and behaviour consistent with that statement. It governs how the crew is introduced at the site, what a shirt, badge or sign-in entry may claim, how the broker answers the direct question of whether these are its own people, what a coverage crew arriving unexpectedly is told to say, and how written communications name the responsible party. The standard is deliberately asymmetric: the broker may promise accountability - that it selects, verifies, inspects and replaces crews, and that the client has one number to call at any hour - but it may never let a uniform, an email signature or a convenient silence imply that the cleaners are its employees when they are not. Where the client's own policy or contract requires knowing exactly who is in the building, disclosure runs further into named personnel lists, badge issuance and whatever background-check class the contract imposes. The rule also runs the other way: a crew is never told to present itself as something the client was never told, because a crew asked to maintain a fiction will eventually say the wrong thing in front of the facility manager, and the damage lands on the broker.

included: what uniforms, badges, sign-in entries and site communications may and may not imply
the answer given when a client asks directly who employs the cleaners
what a coverage or substitute crew is identified as
named-personnel and badge disclosure where the client contract requires it
excluded: the pre-sale disclosure that shaped the buying decision, which the acquisition side owns
the client complaint conversation and its retention consequences
legal conclusions about what disclosure any jurisdiction or contract compels

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client questions who is in the building, or a site practice is found implying employment that does not exist

pros.claim: A single consistent answer removes the recurring risk that a client discovers the model by accident and reads it as concealment
pros.example: a facility manager who asks a crew member who they work for and gets the same answer the broker gave at the sale

pros.claim: Honest framing lets the broker sell what it genuinely provides - selection, verification, inspection and replacement - rather than an identity it cannot support
pros.example: an accountability promise backed by an inspection record, offered instead of an implied claim that the cleaners are staff

cons.claim: Some buyers prefer the impression of a single integrated company and disclosure can cost a deal or invite a direct-hire attempt
cons.example: a client who, on learning the crew is a separate business, asks for the crew's number to contract around the broker

cons.claim: Maintaining consistency across shirts, badges, invoices, signatures and coverage nights is ongoing administrative work that decays without attention
cons.example: a coverage crew arriving in its own branded shirts at a site where the client had only ever seen unbranded ones

failure_modes: letting a uniform, badge or email signature imply employment that does not exist
sending a coverage crew without telling the client the regular crew missed the night
coaching a crew to answer a client question in a way the client was never told
different answers from the salesperson, the inspector and the crew lead to the same question
acceptance_tests: a written one-line answer to the question of who employs the cleaners exists and matches what was said before signing
uniform, badge and sign-in practice at every live site is checked against that answer at least once per inspection cycle
no crew has been instructed to describe the arrangement differently from how the client was told
revisit_triggers: a client asks directly about the service model or about a face they do not recognise
a coverage crew is deployed at a site that has never seen one
the client contract adds named-personnel, badge or background-check requirements

nodes.definition: Before a crew touches a site the broker verifies the coverage obligation classes that the client contract, the landlord, the facility type and the jurisdiction require, treating each as a class to confirm rather than a figure to recall. The classes that commonly appear are general liability; coverage for injury to the people doing the work, which takes the form of workers-compensation or an equivalent occupational-injury arrangement where the crew has workers; a janitorial or fidelity bond class where the client's property and cash exposure warrants one; commercial auto where the crew drives to and between sites; and additional-insured, primary-and-noncontributory or waiver endorsements where the signed client contract demands them. Verification means the certificate arrives from the issuing agent or carrier rather than as a forwarded image, that the named insured is the same entity that signs the crew agreement, that the policy period covers the whole service period, and that the endorsements the client contract actually requires are present rather than presumed. Expiry is treated as a scheduled event with a named owner and a suspension consequence, not as something to remember, because coverage that lapsed in the seventh month is otherwise discovered at the moment of the incident. Whether a given class is legally required for a given arrangement, and whether any limit is adequate, is settled by a licensed insurance professional and counsel in the jurisdiction of performance rather than inside this knowledge base.

included: the coverage and bond obligation classes to confirm per contract and per crew
verification method: issuing agent, entity match, policy period, required endorsements
expiry tracking with a named owner and a suspension rule
flow-down of the client contract's own requirements to the crew agreement
excluded: advice on whether a class is legally required, or on limit adequacy, for any arrangement
the broker's own coverage programme and its placement
claims handling and adjuster negotiation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a certificate approaches expiry, a crew's entity or workforce changes, or a client contract alters its required coverage classes

pros.claim: Verifying with the issuing agent defeats the most common document problems at trivial cost
pros.example: a certificate whose named insured is a personal name while the agreement is signed by a differently named company, caught by a single call before the first shift

pros.claim: Tracked expiry with an automatic suspension rule converts a silent exposure into a scheduled administrative task
pros.example: a renewal date reached with no replacement certificate, which pauses new shifts instead of running an uncovered crew for months

cons.claim: Strict requirements exclude capable small crews that cannot yet carry every class the contract demands, shrinking the supply pool
cons.example: a strong two-person team that has never carried the bond class a client's contract requires and needs time and cost to obtain it

cons.claim: Certificates evidence coverage on a date and prove neither that a policy will respond nor that limits suit the exposure
cons.example: a current certificate on file for a policy whose exclusions were never read by anyone in the transaction

failure_modes: accepting a forwarded image or a screenshot instead of a certificate from the issuing agent
letting the named insured differ from the entity signing the crew agreement without questioning it
filing a certificate without recording its expiry or assigning an owner to the renewal
assuming last year's requirements still match this year's client contract or landlord rules
acceptance_tests: for every live crew there is a current certificate from the issuing agent with the named insured matching the signing entity
the client contract's required classes and endorsements are listed and each is matched to evidence or an open item
every certificate carries a tracked expiry date, a named owner and a written suspension consequence
no output asserts that a class is or is not legally required; each routes to a licensed professional
revisit_triggers: a policy renewal date approaches or passes without a replacement certificate
the crew changes entity, adds workers or begins driving to the site
the client contract or landlord adds or changes a coverage or endorsement requirement

nodes.definition: Crews are small businesses, often owner-operated, frequently thinly capitalised, and sometimes run by people whose commercial experience or command of the contract language is narrower than the broker's, so fair dealing with them is a first-class operating rule here rather than a sentiment. It requires disclosure-first sourcing: the building's real conditions, soil load, access constraints, problem areas and known client sensitivities are told to the crew before the quote rather than discovered on the first shift, the task list handed over is the task list the client bought, and payment terms and timing are stated plainly and then honoured. It forbids the leverage tactics available to whoever holds the client relationship - inventing an urgent competing quote to force a price down, threatening to pull the crew's other sites unless a price is cut, deducting remedies that were never explained, and exploiting a principal's dependence, language, inexperience or immigration status to extract terms they do not understand. Where the counterparty's understanding is visibly limited the duty rises rather than falls: key obligations are explained in plain language and where practical in the language the principal reads, the remedy and termination clauses are walked through before signature, and the crew is told it may take the agreement away and have it reviewed. The self-interested case is identical to the ethical one, which is why it belongs in the operating method: a crew squeezed below sustainability cuts hours at the site, the inspection fails, and the broker pays the difference in coverage cost, remedy work and client risk.

included: disclosure-first sourcing of true site conditions before a quote is requested
the forbidden leverage tactics and why each is also self-defeating
the raised explanation duty where a principal's understanding is limited
payment reliability as an ethical and operational commitment
excluded: client-facing selling ethics, which the acquisition side owns
wage-setting inside the crew's own business and its employment obligations
legal advice on the enforceability or fairness of any specific term

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a crew reports undisclosed conditions, disputes a term it says was never explained, or a payment promise is missed

pros.claim: Full site disclosure before quoting produces prices that survive the term instead of collapsing on contact with reality
pros.example: telling a crew in advance that the building's after-hours dock is locked and trash must travel two floors, so the quote includes the time it actually takes

pros.claim: Reliable, explained payment makes the broker the client crews protect on a short-staffed night
pros.example: a crew choosing to cover a hard Friday for the broker who has always paid on the stated date over a payer who settles late

cons.claim: Refusing leverage means accepting prices a harder negotiator would beat, which narrows the residual on some sites
cons.example: declining to use a rival's unsolicited lower number to reopen an agreed crew price mid-term

cons.claim: Explaining terms carefully and offering review time lengthens onboarding and can look like hesitation to a crew eager to start
cons.example: a principal who wants to sign immediately being asked to take the agreement away first

failure_modes: withholding known problem conditions to obtain a lower quote
using an invented or unrepresentative competing quote as negotiating leverage
applying a remedy or deduction the crew was never shown before it was enforced
treating a language or experience gap as an advantage rather than as a raised duty to explain
acceptance_tests: the site conditions disclosed before the quote match what the crew finds on the first shift
every remedy, deduction and termination term was explained before signature and can be evidenced
payment dates promised to crews match payment dates met, tracked over time
no negotiation record contains a competing quote that was not real
revisit_triggers: a crew reports conditions on the first shift that nobody disclosed
a crew principal signals confusion about a term the broker is about to enforce
the broker's own cash position tempts a delay in paying crews

nodes.definition: Sourcing crews under deadline pressure is how brokers end up with unverified labour on a client's floor, so this unit of work builds the supply picture continuously rather than at the moment of need. It maps the local classes of supply: established independent janitorial companies with their own crews and clients, owner-operator teams working nights, specialty vendors for floor care, carpet extraction, window and post-construction work that a generalist crew would subcontract anyway, day-porter labour that behaves more like staffing than contracting, and the referral network of the crews the broker already uses. For each it records the geography already covered, the nights already worked, headcount and genuine capacity headroom, equipment owned, coverage posture, facility classes already handled, and how the crew was found - because channel predicts behaviour, and a crew referred by a satisfied crew tends to behave differently from one answering an advertisement. Route geography is a first-class field: two buildings a few minutes apart can be staffed by one crew at a cost neither could carry alone, and a crew's existing route is the cheapest capacity in the market. The map is maintained as a living register with contact recency, because a bench is only warm if the people on it have heard from the broker lately and know what kind of work is coming, and a name collected two years ago and never called again is not coverage.

included: classes of local cleaning supply and the channels that surface them
per-crew fields including route geography, nights worked, headcount and capacity headroom
contact recency as the measure of whether a bench is warm
specialty vendor coverage for periodic work the contracts promise
excluded: screening and verifying a specific crew for a specific building
quoting or negotiating price
roster-level concentration decisions across the whole book

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new cluster is sold into, a mapped crew's capacity or route changes, or a referral introduces a supply class the map does not hold

pros.claim: A standing map turns an urgent staffing problem into a call rather than a search
pros.example: a contract starting in eleven days staffed from three crews already mapped as working that side of town on those nights

pros.claim: Route geography recorded in advance reveals cheap capacity that a site-by-site search never finds
pros.example: a small suite that no crew would drive for alone becoming viable because a mapped crew already cleans the building next door

cons.claim: The map decays quickly and maintaining it is unpaid work that competes with selling
cons.example: a register whose capacity and coverage fields were accurate a year ago and are now wrong for half the entries

cons.claim: Breadth invites the temptation to use an unverified mapped crew when time is short
cons.example: reaching for a name on the map that was never screened because the alternative is a missed first night

failure_modes: building the map only when a site needs staffing, so every choice is made under time pressure
recording names and numbers without capacity, geography or coverage posture
letting contact recency lapse so the bench is theoretical
ignoring specialty vendors until a periodic task promised in a contract comes due
acceptance_tests: every geographic cluster the broker sells into has at least one mapped and one alternate crew
each register entry carries nights worked, route geography, headcount, capacity headroom and last contact date
specialty capability for every periodic task the live contracts promise is mapped to a named vendor or crew
revisit_triggers: the broker sells into a cluster with no mapped crew
a mapped crew's capacity, coverage posture or route changes
contact recency on a bench crew passes the interval the broker set

nodes.definition: Before references are called or a quote is requested, a candidate crew is screened against the specific building's demands so that unsuitable candidates are removed while removal is still cheap. The screen asks what the crew currently runs - how many sites, of what facility class, on which nights - and whether it has genuine capacity headroom or is proposing to stretch the same people across another building; who would actually be on this site and whether that person has cleaned this facility class before; what equipment the crew owns, rents or expects to be given; whether it already carries the coverage classes the client contract requires or can obtain them and in what time; how the business is formed and how long it has traded; whether it subcontracts any of its own work onward; and whether it can meet facility-specific requirements such as background-check classes, escort rules, badge protocols and restricted areas. It screens the working relationship as well as the capability, because a crew that will not answer the phone during the screen will not answer it at eleven at night when the alarm trips and the building is open. The output is a recorded fit or no-fit decision with its reason, so that the same unsuitable crew is not re-screened next quarter and so that the pattern in why crews fail the screen feeds back into how the supply map is built.

included: site-specific capability, capacity, equipment, coverage and formation questions
facility-specific requirement screening such as background-check and escort classes
responsiveness as a screened attribute
a recorded fit or no-fit decision with its reason
excluded: verifying the crew's answers against its existing work
price formation and quote comparison
the written agreement and its terms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a screened crew fails in a way the screen did not test for, or a facility class introduces a requirement the screen does not ask about

pros.claim: Screening against the specific building stops a generally good crew being placed where it will predictably fail
pros.example: a strong office crew screened out of a medical suite because nobody on the team has handled regulated waste segregation or the facility's training class

pros.claim: A recorded reason makes the screen cumulative instead of repeated from scratch every time
pros.example: a crew declined for capacity in the spring being revisited deliberately once it reports a hired team rather than being re-asked the same questions

cons.claim: Screens reward crews that present well and can filter out capable operators who are poor at answering questions
cons.example: an excellent night team whose principal is uncomfortable on the phone scoring worse than a polished salesperson who will subcontract the work

cons.claim: Stated capacity headroom is self-reported and optimistic, so the screen measures intention as much as capability
cons.example: a crew that says it has room for one more building because it intends to hire, not because it has hired

failure_modes: screening for general quality rather than fitness for this facility class and these nights
accepting stated capacity without asking how many people exist and where they already work
skipping the onward-subcontracting question and discovering a third party in the building later
leaving the decision unrecorded so the same crew is re-screened repeatedly
acceptance_tests: each screen names the site, the facility class and the nights it was run against
capacity is recorded as headcount and existing commitments rather than as a stated willingness
the onward-subcontracting question is asked and its answer recorded
every screen ends in a written fit or no-fit decision with a reason
revisit_triggers: the crew's headcount, route or existing commitments change materially
a screened-in crew fails on a site in a way the screen should have caught
the client contract adds a facility-specific requirement the screen does not test

nodes.definition: Claims made in a screen are cheap, so this unit of work verifies them against work the crew is already doing. Reference conversations are run with specific rather than general questions - how long have they cleaned for you, what happened the last time someone called in sick, has a night ever been missed and what did they do about it, do the same people show up or is it different faces, who do you call and how quickly do they answer, what have you asked them to fix and did it stay fixed - because a general enquiry about whether they are good produces a useless yes. Where the crew's existing client permits it, the broker visits a building the crew cleans, at or near the hours it is cleaned, and inspects it against the standard it would be held to at the new site: restroom detail, corner and edge work, high-touch surfaces, trash handling, and whether the supply closet is organised or chaotic, which predicts more than most references do. The entity is confirmed as part of the same step - that the trading name, the person who will sign, and the named insured on the certificate are the same party, and that the crew is not itself brokering the work quietly to someone the broker has never seen. Verification is proportionate to consequence, since a small low-sensitivity suite does not justify what a medical or high-security facility demands, but it is never skipped entirely because a start date is close.

included: specific reference questions that produce evidence rather than sentiment
a site visit to work the crew already performs, at or near working hours
entity confirmation across trading name, signatory and named insured
detection of undisclosed onward subcontracting
excluded: the initial fitness screen that precedes it
price negotiation
background-check administration, which the client contract and access control govern

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a verified crew fails in a way references did not predict, or its ownership, entity or lead personnel change

pros.claim: A visit to work the crew already does shows the standard it actually holds rather than the one it describes
pros.example: restroom corners and floor edges inspected in a building the crew has cleaned for two years, which is where habitual shortcuts show

pros.claim: Entity confirmation catches the arrangement that would otherwise put an unverified third party in a client's building
pros.example: a certificate naming a company the signatory does not control, surfaced before any credential is issued

cons.claim: References are volunteered by the crew and therefore selected, and visits depend on another client's goodwill
cons.example: a crew offering only its easiest site and its friendliest contact, with no obligation to mention the account it lost

cons.claim: Thorough verification takes days that a signed contract with a fixed start date may not have
cons.example: a fourteen-day window between signature and first shift that cannot absorb reference calls, a site visit and a coverage check for three candidate crews

failure_modes: asking whether a crew is good instead of asking what happened the last time something went wrong
accepting references without ever seeing work in progress
skipping verification because the start date is close and the crew seemed impressive
failing to confirm that the signatory, the trading entity and the insured are the same party
acceptance_tests: at least one reference conversation records a specific past failure and how the crew handled it
for any site above the broker's stated consequence threshold, a visit to existing work has been made and its observations recorded
the signing entity, trading name and named insured are documented as matching
the crew has stated in writing whether it subcontracts any part of its work onward
revisit_triggers: the crew is proposed for a materially more sensitive facility class than it was verified for
a reference later reports a failure the verification did not surface
the crew's entity, ownership or lead personnel change

nodes.definition: A crew's price is not a market fact to be looked up; it is a number the crew builds from the hours it believes the building takes, the pay it must offer to hold people on that shift, its own overhead, travel and equipment, and whatever margin it needs to survive - and the broker's task is to understand that build well enough to judge whether the number will hold for the whole term. This unit of work normalises the scope before any comparison: every crew quotes against the same task list, the same frequency calendar, the same measured areas and floor mix, the same supplies and equipment split, and the same treatment of periodic work, so that a difference in price means a difference in cost rather than a difference in interpretation. Each quote is then tested against the delivery mandate's costed labour load rather than only against the other quotes, which is what exposes the dangerous case: a price so low that it implies fewer crew-hours than the task list can physically be performed in never becomes a bargain and always becomes a deficiency, a coverage failure or a mid-term demand for more money. The difference between the client price and the crew price is treated as a built residual that must still absorb consumables, inspection time, coverage, remedy and administration, not as the broker's earnings. No price, rate or spread quoted by any party is accepted as an industry norm: each is a number this particular deal produced, recorded in writing against the scope version it was quoted for, and re-verified whenever that scope changes.

included: how a crew builds its own number and what moves it
scope normalisation so quotes are comparable
testing a quote against the costed labour load rather than against rivals alone
recording price against the scope version it was quoted for
excluded: the client-facing price and the bid that produced it
monthly margin tracking and repricing conversations with the client
any statement of what crews or contracts are worth as a market figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a crew requests a price change, delivered hours diverge from the quoted implication, or the scope the quote referenced is amended

pros.claim: Normalised scope makes quote differences informative instead of accidental
pros.example: three crews quoting the same four-visit calendar with the same periodic work and the same supplies split, so the cheapest is genuinely cheaper rather than quoting less work

pros.claim: Testing against the costed labour load catches the unsustainable low quote before it is accepted
pros.example: a number that implies one person covering a building the walkthrough measured for two, recognised as a future failure rather than a win

cons.claim: The crew's internal build is partly opaque and a broker cannot audit another business's cost structure
cons.example: a crew that genuinely runs leaner because the building sits on an existing route being indistinguishable on paper from one that is underpricing

cons.claim: Normalisation and testing slow down quoting and can lose a crew that has other offers on the table
cons.example: a strong crew accepting other work while the broker rebuilds the comparison on a normalised scope

failure_modes: comparing quotes taken against different task lists, frequencies or supplies splits
choosing the lowest number without testing it against the hours the task list requires
treating the client-price-minus-crew-price difference as profit rather than as a residual with obligations
repeating a remembered rate from another deal as though it were a market benchmark
acceptance_tests: every quote in a comparison references the same scope version, frequency calendar and supplies split
each quote is recorded alongside the crew-hours it implies and the costed labour load it is tested against
a quote below the plausible staffing floor is either explained by a documented reason or declined
no figure in the record is presented as a market rate; each is traced to the quote or contract that produced it
revisit_triggers: the client scope, frequency or supplies split changes after quoting
a crew requests a price increase or signals distress
delivered hours at the site diverge from the hours the accepted quote implied

nodes.definition: The written agreement with the crew is where the structure chosen upstream becomes operative language, and it exists to make obligations mutual, legible and enforceable without inventing legal conclusions. It references rather than restates the scope pack, so that a single document governs what done means; it states the payment basis, cycle and timing; it names the coverage classes the crew must carry and keep current and the consequence of a lapse; it fixes the supplies and equipment split; it defines quality by reference to the written standard and the inspection instrument, including how a deficiency is noticed, what correction window applies, how escalation proceeds and exactly how any remedy is calculated; it addresses onward subcontracting explicitly rather than by silence; it sets non-solicitation of the client and of the broker's other crews with a duration and scope that is proportionate rather than punitive; it covers keys, codes, confidentiality and site rules; and it states notice periods on both sides so that a departure can be orderly. Every term that will ever be enforced is explained before signature, because a remedy clause the crew did not understand produces a dispute rather than a deterrent. What the agreement must never do is quietly contradict the engagement structure: a document that reads as an independent-contractor arrangement while the operating pattern behaves otherwise creates the worst of both, which is why the drafting and the structure question are verified together with a qualified professional in the jurisdiction of performance rather than assembled from templates.

included: the term classes a crew agreement must address and why each exists
referencing the scope pack and inspection standard rather than restating them
explaining enforceable terms before signature
keeping agreement language consistent with the verified engagement structure
excluded: drafting or approving legally binding language, which requires counsel in the jurisdiction of performance
the client-facing service contract and its terms
conclusions about enforceability of non-solicitation or remedy provisions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute exposes an unclear term, the engagement structure changes, or a client contract adds a flow-down obligation

pros.claim: Defining quality by reference to the written standard makes enforcement a matter of evidence rather than opinion
pros.example: a deficiency notice that cites the standard clause, the area, the date and the photograph rather than an assertion that the building looked bad

pros.claim: Explicit onward-subcontracting and notice terms make an orderly exit possible instead of a disappearance
pros.example: a crew giving written notice with a defined transition period rather than stopping without warning after a dispute

cons.claim: A thorough agreement intimidates small crews and can cost the broker good operators who read length as risk
cons.example: an owner-operator declining to sign anything longer than a page and taking work from a broker who asks for less

cons.claim: Terms that read well can pull the operating pattern toward control the structure was designed to avoid
cons.example: a clause dictating start times and personnel that makes the paperwork inconsistent with the verified structure

failure_modes: assembling the agreement from an unrelated template without professional review for the jurisdiction
leaving supplies, equipment, remedy calculation or onward subcontracting unaddressed
writing language that contradicts the verified engagement structure
enforcing a term that was never walked through with the crew before signature
acceptance_tests: every term class - payment, coverage, supplies, quality and remedy, subcontracting, non-solicitation, credentials, notice - is either present or consciously excluded with a reason
the agreement references the scope pack version and the written standard rather than paraphrasing them
a professional in the jurisdiction of performance has reviewed the agreement against the chosen engagement structure
a record exists showing the enforceable terms were explained before signature
revisit_triggers: the engagement structure or the operating pattern changes
a term proves unclear or unenforceable in a real dispute
the client contract adds an obligation that must flow down to the crew

nodes.definition: The bid was built from a measured task list and a frequency matrix; this unit of work converts that into something a crew lead can actually work from at eleven at night without telephoning anyone. The pack is site-specific and contains a floor-by-floor, room-by-room task card naming what happens every visit and what happens weekly, monthly and quarterly, with the frequency expressed as a calendar of dates rather than as prose; a marked plan or photo set showing restrooms, break areas, entries, glass, elevator and stair zones, restricted rooms and the areas the client watches closely; the special instructions that came out of the sales walkthrough, such as the office that is never entered, the door that is never propped, the waste stream that is separated, the alarm that must be set by a fixed time; the supply closet location and stock list; and the escalation contacts together with the standing rule that any request from site staff routes to the broker rather than being absorbed by the crew. It preserves the scope's exclusions as loudly as its inclusions, because what the client did not buy is what later arrives as an unpaid expectation. The pack is delivered in a form the crew will actually use, printed and posted in the closet as well as sent electronically, and it is versioned, because an unversioned pack means nobody can say what the crew was told when a deficiency is disputed.

included: room-by-room task cards and a dated frequency calendar
marked plans, restricted areas and client-sensitive zones
special instructions, exclusions, supply location and escalation routing
version control of the pack as the record of what the crew was told
excluded: how to perform any cleaning task, which is the crew's professional method
re-scoping or re-measuring the building, which belongs to the bid
client-facing scope negotiation and change orders

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the building, occupancy or task list changes, or repeated deficiencies at the same area suggest the pack rather than the crew is at fault

pros.claim: A pack a crew can follow unaided removes the first month of avoidable misses
pros.example: a task card that names the third-floor kitchen and the loading dock landing, which a verbal brief would have omitted and the client would have noticed in week one

pros.claim: Stated exclusions protect the crew and the price from absorbed extras
pros.example: interior window washing above reach height printed as excluded, so a facility manager's casual request routes to the broker as a priced add-on

cons.claim: A highly prescriptive pack edges toward directing the manner of work and must be written as outcomes and site rules rather than as method
cons.example: a card that specifies which machine and chemical to use rather than the observable result required

cons.claim: Packs decay as buildings change and a stale pack is worse than none because it is trusted
cons.example: a suite reconfigured into open plan while the task card still lists offices that no longer exist

failure_modes: handing over the proposal instead of a crew-usable instruction set
omitting exclusions so unbought work is absorbed and then expected
leaving the pack unversioned so a disputed deficiency has no reference
writing method instructions that direct how the crew works rather than what must be observable
acceptance_tests: the pack lists every area the bid measured, with per-visit, weekly, monthly and periodic tasks on a dated calendar
exclusions and restricted areas appear explicitly and in the same document as the inclusions
the pack carries a version number and date and a copy is posted at the site
the escalation rule routing site-staff requests to the broker is stated in the pack
revisit_triggers: the building changes layout, occupancy, hours or waste handling
the client adds, removes or reprices a task
the same task is missed at the site by successive crews, which suggests a specification defect

nodes.definition: Access is the part of delivery where a small administrative lapse becomes a security incident and an indefensible conversation with a client, so it is run as a controlled register rather than as a habit. Every credential issued to a crew - keys, fobs, badges, alarm codes, gate remotes, elevator cards and any client system login - is recorded at the moment of issue with the person who received it, the date and the return condition, and codes are individual wherever the client's system allows it so that an entry log means something after the fact. The register carries the facility's own access rules alongside the credentials: escort requirements, permitted hours, sign-in books, camera zones, rooms no crew member enters, and any background-check or vetting class the client contract imposes on people who hold credentials. Recovery is designed before it is needed: the crew agreement makes return a condition of final payment, replacement, rekey and code-change costs are allocated in writing, and any crew change triggers an audit of every credential on the register before the incoming crew is issued anything. When a credential cannot be accounted for the rule is that the lock or the code changes before the next shift and the client is told, because the alternative is hoping, and hoping is the one option that cannot be defended once something goes missing from the building.

included: issuance register for keys, fobs, badges, codes and logins with holder and date
individual codes where the client system supports them
facility access rules, escort requirements and restricted rooms
credential audit on crew change and the unaccounted-credential rule
excluded: designing or administering the client's security systems
conducting background checks, which are an obligation class verified per contract and jurisdiction
the crew's internal personnel decisions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a credential is lost or unreturned, crew personnel change, or the client alters its access, badge or escort rules

pros.claim: A register maintained at the moment of issue makes a crew change auditable instead of approximate
pros.example: an outgoing crew handing back four fobs against a register that shows five were issued, which is discovered before the incoming crew starts

pros.claim: Individual codes convert an entry log into evidence about a specific night
pros.example: a disputed missed visit resolved by showing which code opened the building and when

cons.claim: Rekey and code-change costs are real and land on whoever the agreement says, which makes the strict rule expensive to honour
cons.example: a lost master key on a multi-tenant floor forcing a rekey the crew cannot afford and the broker must fund to keep the client whole

cons.claim: Individual credentials add administration the client's own system may not support
cons.example: a building whose alarm panel holds one shared code for the whole cleaning contract, so attribution is impossible whatever the register says

failure_modes: handing over keys informally at a walkthrough and never recording who has what
using a single shared alarm code across crews and turnover so no entry can be attributed
letting a crew change happen without a credential audit
deciding not to rekey after an unaccounted credential because of cost
acceptance_tests: every credential in use at a live site maps to a named holder and an issue date in the register
the agreement states who pays for replacement, rekey and code change
a crew change cannot be closed until the credential audit is complete
an unaccounted credential has triggered a rekey or code change and a client notification
revisit_triggers: a crew member with credentials leaves the crew
a credential is reported lost or cannot be accounted for at audit
the client changes locks, codes, badge policy or escort rules

nodes.definition: The joint walkthrough is the highest-yield hour on the delivery side: the broker, the crew lead and, where the client will attend, the facility contact walk the building together against the scope pack before the first billed shift. Its purpose is calibration. The crew sees what clean means in this particular building - which corners the client actually looks at, where the difficult floor transitions and the perpetually marked glass are, how waste leaves the building and by which route, where the supplies live, and what the lockup and alarm sequence is. It also fixes the operational facts that cause first-month failures: the real start time, how many people will arrive, who the lead is, how completion will be confirmed each night, and what happens on a public holiday or a night the building is occupied late. Where the client attends it doubles as the disclosure moment, because the client meets the crew as the contracted crew the broker arranged, which removes in advance the ambiguity a later coverage visit would otherwise create. A transition from an incumbent adds one further task: documenting the building's condition on the day of handover with dated photographs, so that inherited neglect is neither scored against the new crew nor left to surface later as a complaint that nobody can date.

included: the joint pre-service walk against the scope pack with the crew lead
calibration of the standard on the actual building
operational facts: start time, headcount, lead, completion confirmation, holidays
dated condition documentation at handover from an incumbent
excluded: the sales walkthrough that produced the measured scope and the bid
training the crew in cleaning method
the client complaint conversation and its retention handling

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: crew personnel or the building change, or early deficiencies cluster in areas the walkthrough was meant to calibrate

pros.claim: Walking the building together converts a written standard into a shared reference the crew has actually seen
pros.example: showing the lobby glass at the height hands touch it and the stair edges the client mentioned, which no document conveys as well as pointing

pros.claim: Dated handover photographs stop inherited condition from being charged to the incoming crew or discovered later as a surprise
pros.example: a carpet already stained before the new crew started, photographed on the handover date and raised with the client immediately

cons.claim: The walkthrough is scheduled in the client's building and the crew's working hours, so it is easy to postpone into non-existence
cons.example: a start date that lands on a holiday week with the facility contact away, so the walk is skipped and the standard is never calibrated

cons.claim: Calibrating in person invites the broker to demonstrate technique, which drifts from specifying outcomes into directing method
cons.example: showing a crew how to run the mop rather than what the finished floor must look like

failure_modes: starting service without any joint walk because the contract start date arrived
walking the building without the scope pack in hand, so nothing is calibrated against the document
failing to document existing condition at a handover from an incumbent
letting the walk become a method demonstration rather than a standard calibration
acceptance_tests: the walk happened before the first billed shift and its date, attendees and observations are recorded
start time, crew headcount, named lead and the nightly completion confirmation method are agreed and written down
for a transition, dated photographs of the building's condition on the handover day exist
the crew lead has the current pack version in hand during the walk
revisit_triggers: the crew lead or the majority of the crew's people change
the building changes hours, layout, occupancy or waste routing
early inspections show misses concentrated where calibration should have prevented them

nodes.definition: Clean is not a standard; an inspectable standard states, per area type and per task, what an inspector must be able to observe for that task to count as done. This unit of work writes that instrument from the contracted task list: restroom fixtures free of visible soil and water spotting with dispensers stocked and floors detailed at the edges rather than only down the traffic lane; hard-floor corners and edges free of build-up; carpet free of visible debris with entry mats lifted and the floor beneath them cleaned; high-touch surfaces wiped rather than passed over; waste liners changed on the stated rule rather than when visibly full; glass free of hand marks at the heights people actually touch. It draws a deliberate line between standards and methods: the broker specifies observable outcomes and the safety and site rules that bind the work and leaves method, chemistry and sequence to the crew as an independent business, a boundary that serves both the quality of the instrument and the structural question upstream. It names tolerances explicitly, because an unstated tolerance is argued about at the worst possible moment, and it distinguishes a recurring deficiency from a one-off event so that a score describes the system rather than one night. The standard is written once per facility class and then tuned per site, since what a medical suite requires and what a warehouse office requires are genuinely different observations rather than different levels of effort.

included: observable per-task, per-area-type acceptance statements
explicit tolerances and the recurring-versus-one-off distinction
per-facility-class standards tuned to the individual site
the outcome-not-method boundary
excluded: cleaning method, chemical selection and equipment technique
the client contract's own service-level language, which the acquisition side negotiated
scoring weights and the inspection instrument itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deficiencies are disputed as unspecified, or a client is dissatisfied at a site whose scores pass the written standard

pros.claim: An observable statement makes disagreement resolvable by looking rather than by arguing
pros.example: an entry mat lifted during inspection because the standard says the floor beneath it is cleaned, which is either true or not on the night

pros.claim: Specifying outcomes rather than methods respects the crew as an independent business while still binding quality
pros.example: requiring a streak-free glass result at hand height without naming the cloth, chemical or sequence used to achieve it

cons.claim: Written tolerances can be gamed toward the minimum, producing technically compliant buildings clients still dislike
cons.example: a crew meeting every stated observation while the overall impression on a Monday morning remains poor

cons.claim: Standards written per facility class take real effort and go stale as buildings and client expectations change
cons.example: a standard written for a lightly occupied office that no longer matches the same suite after headcount doubled

failure_modes: defining quality as a percentage without saying what is observed
writing method instructions into the standard and creating direction the structure did not intend
leaving tolerances unstated so every deficiency becomes a negotiation
using one generic standard across facility classes with genuinely different requirements
acceptance_tests: each contracted task has an observable acceptance statement an inspector can check on site
tolerances and the recurring-versus-one-off rule are written rather than implied
the standard contains no instruction on method, chemistry or equipment technique
the crew received the standard before the first billed shift and acknowledged it
revisit_triggers: deficiencies are repeatedly disputed on the ground that the standard did not say so
the client expresses dissatisfaction at a site whose scores are passing
occupancy, use or facility class of the building changes

nodes.definition: Inspection time is the broker's scarcest resource, so cadence is allocated by consequence rather than spread evenly across the book. This unit of work sets the frequency and type of walkthrough per site from a small set of drivers: how new the account and the crew are, the facility class and how visible or regulated its cleanliness is, contract value and how hard the site would be to replace, deficiency and complaint history, how recently the crew's staffing changed, and whether periodic work is due for verification. New accounts and new crews receive a dense early cadence that decays as scores stabilise; a crew with a clean record at a low-sensitivity site earns a lighter touch; any deficiency, staffing change or client concern resets the cadence to the dense pattern. Announced and unannounced visits are mixed deliberately, and the hour is varied, because an inspection always performed on a Monday morning measures the Friday shift and nothing else. Cadence design also respects the structural boundary drawn upstream: inspections observe and score outcomes against the agreed standard and are scheduled around the crew's own business rather than used as a mechanism to direct how the crew works, and any drift toward continuous on-site supervision is a signal to re-verify the engagement structure rather than a quality victory.

included: risk drivers that set per-site inspection frequency
decay and reset rules as scores stabilise or deteriorate
announced versus unannounced mix and varied inspection hours
periodic-work verification timing
excluded: the scoring instrument and its weights
the corrective ladder that follows a failed inspection
client-facing quality reporting and retention conversations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deficiency, staffing change or client concern fires the reset rule, or the broker's available inspection capacity changes

pros.claim: Risk weighting puts the broker's limited hours where a failure would actually cost the most
pros.example: a newly transitioned medical suite walked several times in its first weeks while a stable low-sensitivity office on a long-tenured crew is walked far less often

pros.claim: Varying the hour and the announcement makes the measurement representative rather than ceremonial
pros.example: an unannounced visit late in the week that shows what the building looks like at its worst point in the cycle

cons.claim: Decaying cadence on a stable site is exactly how a slow deterioration goes unseen until a client raises it
cons.example: a long-quiet account whose crew quietly halved its hours after a staffing change nobody was told about

cons.claim: Denser inspection consumes hours the residual has to pay for and can look like supervision rather than verification
cons.example: several inspections a week at a site whose spread cannot carry that much of the broker's time

failure_modes: inspecting every site at the same interval regardless of consequence
always inspecting at the same hour so the measurement covers one shift only
failing to reset the cadence after a staffing change or a deficiency
letting inspection frequency become continuous supervision without re-examining the engagement structure
acceptance_tests: each live site has a written cadence with the drivers that set it
the reset rule after a deficiency, staffing change or client concern is stated and has been applied
inspection records show variation in day and hour rather than a single repeated slot
periodic contracted work has a scheduled verification rather than being assumed done
revisit_triggers: a deficiency, complaint or staffing change occurs at the site
the account or the crew passes the newness threshold the cadence decays on
the broker's own available inspection hours change materially

nodes.definition: A score is only useful if the same building inspected by two people on the same night produces nearly the same number, so this unit of work builds both the instrument and the discipline that makes that true. It defines the scored units - area types weighted by how much the client cares about them and how much of the contract's labour they consume, so that restrooms and entries carry more weight than a storage corridor - and it fixes what each observation records: the area, the task, pass or deficiency, a dated photograph for every deficiency, and a short factual note. It reports trend rather than a single figure, because one poor night after a staffing change and a slow four-week slide are different problems calling for different responses. It guards explicitly against the failure modes that make scores lie: an inspector who marks generously to avoid a difficult conversation, inspections that always happen at the easiest hour, scores written from memory in the car afterwards, and the drift that accumulates when one person inspects alone for a long period without a calibration pass against a second inspector or against the written standard.
