The evidence rule is strict because everything downstream leans on it: a deficiency without a dated photograph and an area reference does not enter the record, and the record is exactly what the crew is shown when a remedy is triggered and what the renewal decision is later argued from.

included: weighted area types and what each observation must record
the dated-photograph evidence rule for deficiencies
trend reporting rather than single-score reporting
inspector calibration against a second inspector or the written standard
excluded: setting the inspection frequency
the corrective action that follows a failed score
client-facing quality reporting formats and retention use of the data

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: two inspectors diverge on the same building, or passing scores coexist with client dissatisfaction

pros.claim: Weighting by client sensitivity and labour share makes the number mean what the client experiences
pros.example: an entry lobby and restrooms dominating the score at a professional office rather than being averaged away by a dozen clean corridors

pros.claim: A photograph-and-date rule turns a disputed impression into a fact both parties can look at
pros.example: a crew disputing a restroom deficiency until shown the dated image of the fixture from that night

cons.claim: Scores drift with the inspector and can become a ritual number that tracks the inspector's mood rather than the building
cons.example: one person inspecting the same route for a year, whose passing threshold has quietly moved without anyone noticing

cons.claim: A well-scoring building can still disappoint a client, because the instrument measures what it was designed to observe
cons.example: consistently passing scores at a site whose occupant complains about an odour nobody wrote an observation for

failure_modes: recording scores from memory after leaving the building
logging deficiencies without photographs or area references
letting one inspector work indefinitely without calibration
reporting a single headline score with no trend and no underlying observations
acceptance_tests: every recorded deficiency carries an area, a task, a date and a photograph
area weights are written down and reflect client sensitivity and labour share
scores are reported as a trend across inspections rather than as one number
a calibration pass against a second inspector or the written standard has occurred within the interval the broker set
revisit_triggers: scores stay high while client dissatisfaction appears
two inspectors produce materially different scores for the same building
the standard or the contracted task list changes

nodes.definition: When an inspection finds a deficiency this unit of work runs the ladder that turns it into a correction rather than a grievance. The first rung is documentation and notice: the specific area, task, date, photograph and the standard clause that was missed, delivered to the crew lead in writing and in the language they work in, with a correction window sized to the deficiency - a missed restroom detail is corrected on the next shift, a floor-care failure may need a scheduled return with equipment. The second rung is re-inspection against the same record, which is what makes the loop closed rather than performative; an unchecked correction is an assumption. The third is escalation exactly as the agreement describes it: a documented pattern, a formal written notice, and only then a remedy calculated as the agreement states, applied prospectively and explained beforehand rather than appearing as a surprise deduction from money already earned. The fourth rung is the decision to stop correcting, which hands off to failure diagnosis rather than repeating the ladder indefinitely. Two boundaries matter here: the loop is driven by the broker's own inspection evidence, and the client-facing complaint conversation with everything it implies for retention belongs to the margin and retention side of the business, which this loop feeds with dated facts rather than replaces.

included: written deficiency notice with evidence and the standard clause missed
correction windows sized to the deficiency type
re-inspection that closes the loop
written escalation and prospective, pre-explained remedy
excluded: the client complaint intake and response system, which the retention side owns
the decision to replace the crew, which failure diagnosis owns
renegotiating the crew price as a substitute for correction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a corrected deficiency recurs, a remedy is disputed, or deficiency patterns point at the specification rather than the crew

pros.claim: A documented, evidenced notice with a sized window fixes most deficiencies without any relationship damage
pros.example: a photographed restroom miss corrected on the next shift and closed at re-inspection, with nothing else required

pros.claim: Re-inspection is what distinguishes a system from a complaint, because it proves the fix rather than assuming it
pros.example: a floor-edge build-up marked corrected by the crew and found unchanged when the same area is checked a week later

cons.claim: The ladder consumes the broker's inspection hours twice for every deficiency and the residual pays for both visits
cons.example: three re-inspections in a month at one site absorbing time budgeted for the rest of the book

cons.claim: Financial remedies against a thin-margin crew can trigger the failure they were meant to prevent
cons.example: a deduction that leaves a small crew unable to pay its people, producing the missed shift the remedy was designed to deter

failure_modes: issuing verbal complaints with no record, so no pattern can ever be shown
assuming a correction happened without re-inspecting
applying a deduction retroactively or without the explanation the agreement requires
running the ladder repeatedly on a crew whose problem is structural rather than correctable
acceptance_tests: every deficiency notice cites area, task, date, photograph and the standard clause missed
each notice carries a correction window and a scheduled re-inspection
any remedy applied matches the agreement's calculation and was explained before it was applied
a documented rule states how many cycles precede handing off to failure diagnosis
revisit_triggers: the same deficiency recurs after a closed correction
a remedy is disputed as unexplained or miscalculated
the pattern of deficiencies suggests the specification rather than the crew is at fault

nodes.definition: Who buys the paper, the liners and the soap, and who owns the vacuums, the burnisher and the auto-scrubber, is decided explicitly before the crew prices the building, because every unstated assumption here returns as a mid-term cost argument. The common patterns are client-supplied consumables with the crew bringing only its own chemicals and small tools, broker-supplied consumables built into the monthly price, and crew-supplied everything with the quote built accordingly - and each behaves differently. Client-supplied removes a variable from the broker entirely but exposes the crew to stock-outs it cannot fix and the client to blame it will direct at the broker anyway. Broker-supplied gives control over product quality and brand consistency and makes consumption a live margin variable that must be watched against occupancy rather than assumed stable. Crew-supplied simplifies the broker's month and pushes both cost and control outward. Equipment is decided separately from consumables because it carries a second consequence: equipment provided by the broker is one of the factor classes a classification analysis weighs, and specialty machines for periodic work are usually better rented or subcontracted to a vendor who owns and maintains them than bought to stand idle between quarterly visits. The model also records restock triggers and who reports them, damage and maintenance responsibility, and what happens to broker-owned equipment when a crew is replaced.

included: the responsibility patterns for consumables and their differing cost behaviour
equipment ownership decided separately, including its classification-factor consequence
restock triggers, reporting duty, damage and maintenance responsibility
disposition of broker-owned equipment on crew replacement
excluded: product and chemical selection, which is the crew's professional method
the client-facing price of supplies, which the bid set
monthly consumable cost tracking as a margin mechanism, which the retention side owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: consumable usage diverges from occupancy, the client alters its supply arrangement, or equipment provision changes and touches the classification question

pros.claim: Deciding the split before quoting removes the most common mid-term cost dispute entirely
pros.example: a crew that assumed the client stocked liners and the broker who assumed the crew did, settled on paper before either priced anything

pros.claim: Separating the equipment decision from the consumables decision keeps a cost choice from quietly becoming a structural one
pros.example: choosing to rent a periodic-use machine rather than supply one to the crew permanently, after seeing which factor class provision touches

cons.claim: Broker-supplied consumables convert a fixed arrangement into a variable cost that must actually be watched
cons.example: consumption at a site rising far faster than occupancy explains, unnoticed for months because nobody owned the comparison

cons.claim: Client-supplied arrangements leave the broker accountable for a stock-out it cannot control
cons.example: an empty dispenser on a Monday because the client's own ordering lapsed, reported to the broker as a cleaning failure

failure_modes: leaving the split to be discovered on the first shift
providing equipment to crews without considering the classification factor it touches
buying specialty machines that stand idle between periodic visits
failing to define who reports a low stock level and to whom
acceptance_tests: the consumables and equipment split is written in the agreement and matches what was quoted
restock triggers, the reporting route and the responsible party are stated
equipment provision decisions record the classification factor they touch and the verification they were checked against
disposition of broker-owned equipment on crew change is written down
revisit_triggers: consumable usage diverges from what the site's occupancy explains
the client changes its own supply arrangements or product preferences
equipment provision changes, which touches the classification question

nodes.definition: A crew will eventually not show up, and the broker's entire differentiation rests on what happens in the next few hours, so coverage is engineered before the first shift rather than improvised on the night. The system has four parts. Detection comes first: a nightly completion confirmation the crew sends and an exception that surfaces when it does not arrive, so the broker learns from its own process rather than from a client's morning telephone call. Second is a named alternate for each site that has already received the scope pack summary, has agreed terms for emergency work in advance, and knows how it would get into the building. Third is an access path that does not depend on the absent crew, because a backup team standing outside a locked building is not coverage; this means a broker-held credential, a client-side arrangement or a lockbox protocol agreed with the client in writing. Fourth is a client communication rule that fixes who is told what and when, and that the answer is truthful. Coverage costs more than the regular crew and that cost lands on the site's residual, which is exactly why the design decides in advance which buildings justify a standby arrangement and which are covered by a best-efforts call list. The rule that must never bend is what the client is told: a coverage crew is identified as a coverage crew, and a missed night is reported rather than hidden, because a client who later discovers a concealed missed shift treats the relationship as finished.

included: nightly completion confirmation and exception detection
named pre-briefed alternates with agreed emergency terms
an access path independent of the absent crew
truthful client notification and the tiering of which sites justify standby cost
excluded: the diagnosis of why the crew failed and whether to replace it
the client retention conversation that may follow a missed night
the crew's own internal staffing and sickness arrangements

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a coverage event occurs, a named alternate becomes unavailable, or the site's access arrangements change

pros.claim: Detection by the broker's own confirmation turns a client-discovered failure into a broker-managed event
pros.example: an absent completion message at midnight triggering a call while there are still hours before the building opens

pros.claim: A pre-briefed alternate with an independent access path makes coverage a phone call rather than a search and a locksmith
pros.example: a bench crew that already holds the site summary and can be let in through a broker-held credential arriving before morning

cons.claim: Standby readiness costs money on nights nothing goes wrong and the residual carries it
cons.example: an agreed retainer-style arrangement at a high-consequence site that is unused for months at a time

cons.claim: A coverage crew does not know the building and its work is usually visibly worse, which itself creates a client conversation
cons.example: an alternate team missing the third-floor kitchen because the site summary is not the same as having walked the building

failure_modes: learning about a missed night from the client rather than from a confirmation process
naming a backup that has never seen the site summary or agreed terms
relying on an access path that runs through the crew that failed to appear
concealing a missed shift or presenting a coverage crew as the regular crew
acceptance_tests: every live site has a named alternate that has received the site summary and agreed emergency terms
an access path independent of the regular crew exists and is documented for each site
a nightly completion confirmation and its exception rule are in operation
the client notification rule states who is told what and within what time, and it has been followed on every missed night
revisit_triggers: a coverage event occurs, whether or not it was handled well
the named alternate becomes unavailable, moves or loses capacity
the client changes access arrangements that the coverage path depends on

nodes.definition: When a crew is failing, the expensive mistake is to replace it without diagnosing why, because several of the causes recur with the next crew unless the underlying condition changes. This unit of work separates them: a quote that was never sustainable for the labour the building needs; a crew that has taken on more sites than its people can hold; staffing churn that removed everyone who attended the onboarding walkthrough; site conditions materially worse than what was scoped, which is a bid finding rather than a crew fault; a scope that grew through on-site requests nobody priced; a business or personal collapse on the crew's side; and a plain mismatch between the crew's real capability and the facility class. The diagnosis chooses among three actions - change the condition and keep the crew, coach against a defined correction window with re-inspection, or replace - and records which was chosen and why, so that the same misdiagnosis is not repeated at the next site. Replacement itself is a sequence rather than an event: secure coverage first, then run the credential audit and any rekey or code change, then make the client notification that matches what actually happened, then onboard the incoming crew with the building documented on the handover day, then close terms with the outgoing crew and pay what the agreement says is owed. A replacement executed in the wrong order is how a broker loses a client and a key on the same night.

included: separating the recurring causes of crew failure
the three-way choice between changing the condition, coaching and replacing
the ordered replacement sequence including credential audit and client notification
closing terms fairly with the outgoing crew
excluded: the decision to exit the client contract itself, which the retention side owns
the deficiency ladder that precedes diagnosis
legal advice on termination, notice or final payment obligations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a replacement crew repeats the predecessor's failure, or a transition exposes a gap in the replacement sequence

pros.claim: Diagnosing cause before replacing stops the broker importing the same failure with a new crew
pros.example: a building failing because the scope grew through unpriced on-site requests, which the next crew would also fail until the requests are priced or refused

pros.claim: An ordered replacement sequence protects the client relationship and the building at the same time
pros.example: coverage arranged and credentials audited before the outgoing crew is told, so no night is missed and no key is unaccounted for

cons.claim: Diagnosis takes time the client's patience may not have, and a slow correct process can still lose the account
cons.example: a facility manager who has already escalated internally and wants a visible change this week rather than a considered one next month

cons.claim: Replacement destroys accumulated building knowledge and the new crew's early scores usually dip
cons.example: a transition where the incoming crew misses the same awkward areas the outgoing crew had eventually learned

failure_modes: replacing the crew when the real cause was an underscoped bid or unpriced scope growth
telling the crew before coverage and credentials are secured
leaving the client to discover the change from a new face in the building
withholding final payment beyond what the agreement provides as informal punishment
acceptance_tests: every replacement decision records the diagnosed cause and why coaching or condition change was rejected
coverage is confirmed and the credential audit is complete before the outgoing crew is notified
the client notification matches the facts and precedes the first unfamiliar face in the building
final payment to the outgoing crew follows the agreement rather than the mood of the exit
revisit_triggers: a replacement crew fails in the same way as its predecessor
the diagnosed cause was a bid or scope condition that has not been corrected
a transition produces a credential, access or client-communication problem

nodes.definition: The roster of crews is a portfolio with exposures, and this unit of work manages it as one rather than as a stack of unrelated relationships. The exposures it tracks are concentration, meaning how much of the book a single crew holds, so that one notice letter or one business failure is not an extinction event; capacity headroom, meaning whether the crews carrying the most sites have any slack left to absorb a coverage night; geographic coverage, meaning whether every cluster the broker sells into has at least one qualified crew and one credible alternate; capability coverage, meaning whether the specialty work the live contracts promise can actually be staffed when it comes due; and leverage balance, because a crew that depends on the broker for nearly all its revenue is fragile and easy to squeeze while a crew for whom the broker is a rounding error will deprioritise the site on a difficult night. It also watches the reverse dependency the broker creates in itself: the crew that holds all the institutional knowledge of an awkward building is a single point of failure, which is why scope packs, credential registers, standards and inspection records live with the broker rather than in a crew lead's memory. Portfolio decisions are made when adding a site rather than when losing one, so the question of who else could hold this building next month is asked before the first crew is ever signed to it.

included: concentration, headroom, geographic and capability coverage across the roster
leverage balance in both directions
keeping institutional site knowledge with the broker rather than the crew
asking the replaceability question before a site is assigned
excluded: screening or verifying an individual crew
client-side account concentration and book composition, which the retention side owns
the crew's own business strategy and client mix

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a crew's share of the book crosses the stated threshold, a crew exits, or new work is won where no alternate exists

pros.claim: Tracking concentration converts a hidden single point of failure into a managed exposure
pros.example: noticing that one crew holds a large share of the book before that crew gives notice rather than during the week it does

pros.claim: Keeping packs, standards and registers with the broker means a crew change transfers a building rather than restarting it
pros.example: an incoming crew receiving the same versioned pack, credential register and standard the outgoing crew worked to

cons.claim: Deliberately spreading work across more crews raises coordination cost and can weaken the relationship with the best operator
cons.example: splitting a cluster between two crews so neither gets the route density that made the price work

cons.claim: A crew that senses it is being managed as an exposure may reduce its own commitment
cons.example: an operator who notices work being diverted to an alternate and begins prioritising other clients

failure_modes: letting one crew accumulate a large share of the book unnoticed
assigning a site with no credible alternate anywhere in that geography
leaving the only knowledge of an awkward building inside one crew lead's head
promising specialty periodic work in contracts with no mapped capability to deliver it
acceptance_tests: the share of sites held by each crew is recorded and reviewed on a stated interval
every live site has at least one named alternate crew that could hold it
packs, standards, credential registers and inspection records are held by the broker for every site
every specialty periodic obligation in a live contract maps to a named crew or vendor
revisit_triggers: a crew's share of the book passes the threshold the broker set
a crew gives notice, loses capacity or fails
the broker wins work in a cluster with no qualified alternate

nodes.definition: Everything the delivery side learns has to survive in a form other decisions can use, so this unit of work defines that record and the gate that closes the delivery loop. Per crew it holds the engagement structure and the agreement version, the verification log for the classification question with the professional consulted and the date, current certificates with their expiry dates and the suspension rule, the sites held and their start dates, the quoted price history against the scope version each price was quoted for, inspection scores over time with their deficiencies and closures, coverage failures and how each was resolved, credential issuance and recovery, and any client feedback that reached the broker. Per site it holds the scope pack version, the written standard, the current cadence and the crew presently assigned. The record exists to make three downstream decisions evidence-based rather than anecdotal: which crew receives the next building, whether a crew's request for a price increase is supportable, and whether the site's delivered cost and delivered quality still support the contract - the last of which is handed to the margin, retention and renewal side of the business rather than decided here. The gate is explicit and checkable: a site is not considered fully transitioned until the pack, the standard, the certificates, the credential register, the coverage arrangement and the first completed inspection all exist in the record.

included: the per-crew and per-site fields the record must carry
the three downstream decisions the record serves
the transition completeness gate
the handoff of delivered cost and quality evidence to the margin and retention side
excluded: the renewal, repricing and exit decisions themselves
client-facing reporting formats and account reviews
storing personal data about crew workers beyond what credentialing and contract flow-down require

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a downstream renewal, repricing or assignment question cannot be answered from the record, or an audit finds a gated item missing at a live site

pros.claim: A single record makes the next site assignment an evidence decision rather than a recollection
pros.example: choosing between two crews for a demanding building by comparing their inspection trends, coverage failures and deficiency closures rather than by impression

pros.claim: The transition gate stops half-finished onboardings from being treated as complete
pros.example: a site running for weeks without a certificate on file or a first inspection, which the gate catches before it becomes routine

cons.claim: The record is administrative work with no immediate revenue and it is the first thing abandoned in a busy month
cons.example: certificates and credential entries left un-updated across a quarter of heavy selling, discovered only when a crew has to be replaced

cons.claim: A record is only as honest as the inspections behind it, so a generous inspector produces a confident but misleading history
cons.example: a crew with an unblemished record that was never inspected at a demanding hour

failure_modes: keeping crew history in memory and email threads rather than in a record
declaring a site transitioned before the certificate, coverage arrangement or first inspection exists
recording scores without the deficiencies and closures that explain them
holding more personal data about crew workers than credentialing and contract flow-down require
acceptance_tests: for each crew the record holds agreement version, verification log, current certificates with expiries, sites, price history, score trend, deficiencies, coverage events and credentials
for each site the record holds pack version, standard, cadence and current crew
no site is marked transitioned until pack, standard, certificates, credential register, coverage arrangement and first inspection are all present
the delivered cost and quality summary handed to the margin and retention side is generated from this record rather than from recollection
revisit_triggers: a certificate expiry, crew change or coverage event occurs and must be written into the record
a downstream renewal or repricing question cannot be answered from the record
an audit finds a live site missing one of the gated items

edges.why_related: the structure question is asked about a specific delivery obligation: what has to be delivered, how often and under whose direction is what the factor classes are mapped against
what the client was promised on the delivery side is what every later introduction, badge and coverage visit must stay consistent with
which coverage classes are even applicable depends on whether the people cleaning are the broker's workers or an independent business with its own workers
the screen runs against candidates the supply map has already surfaced, so a thin map produces a screen with nothing to choose between
the coverage classes the client contract requires become screening questions, so a crew that cannot carry them is removed before anyone spends time on references
verification exists to test the specific claims the screen collected, so it needs the screen's answers to have something to check
only screened-in crews are asked to quote, because a quote from a crew that cannot hold the building wastes the comparison and anchors the broker on an unusable number
the agreement records the accepted price, the scope version it was quoted against and the payment basis, none of which exist until the quote is settled
the agreement is the operative expression of the chosen structure, so drafting before the structure is verified produces language that has to be rewritten
the pack is the document the agreement references as the definition of done, so the agreement must exist and point at a versioned pack
the joint walk calibrates the crew against the pack, so walking a building without the pack in hand calibrates nothing
the observable acceptance statements are written for the tasks and areas the pack enumerates, so the standard cannot be written before the pack fixes them
there is nothing to inspect against until the standard states what an inspector must observe, so cadence without a standard produces visits rather than measurements
the remedy ladder is driven by scored, evidenced observations, and an unevidenced complaint cannot start it
the supplies and equipment split is a term of the agreement rather than a habit, so it is settled where the obligations are written
diagnosis begins where the corrective ladder stops working, and it uses the ladder's documented history as its evidence
replacement cannot begin until coverage exists, because the first step of the sequence is protecting the nights between the two crews
the record carries the roster-level exposures alongside per-crew history, so the portfolio view has to exist before the record can report it
the introduction at the joint walk is the moment the service model is either confirmed or blurred, so the disclosure rule bounds how the crew is presented
edges.risk_of_conflict: a client who wants a single-company impression can pull the introduction toward implying employment

edges.why_related: fair dealing bounds how a quote may be sought and negotiated: full site disclosure before quoting, no invented competing numbers, no threats to withdraw other sites
no pack, credential or start date is released until the required coverage classes are verified, which makes coverage a gate on the handoff rather than a parallel task
who provides equipment and consumables is one of the factor classes a classification analysis weighs, so the supplies decision is bounded by the verified structure
every enforceable term must be explained before signature and be proportionate rather than punitive, which constrains what the agreement may contain and how it is presented
tighter and more frequent on-site presence improves quality control but moves the relationship toward the direction and schedule-control factors a classification analysis weighs
edges.resolution_rule: the verified structure wins: inspections observe and score outcomes against the written standard and may be made denser or unannounced, but they may not become continuous direction of how or when the crew works; if quality genuinely requires that level of direction, the structure itself is re-verified with a qualified professional before the practice becomes routine

edges.why_related: the cheapest acceptable crew price and the standard the building must be held to pull against each other, because a price below the plausible staffing floor cannot produce the observations the standard requires
edges.resolution_rule: the standard wins: a quote that implies fewer crew-hours than the task list can physically be performed in is declined or re-scoped rather than accepted and policed, and if no crew will hold the standard at a price the signed contract can carry, that is escalated as a bid and margin finding rather than absorbed by lowering what is inspected

edges.why_related: keeping alternates warm enough to cover a failed night means courting crews the incumbent regards as rivals, while consolidating the book with one strong crew is cheaper and simpler but fragile
edges.resolution_rule: coverage readiness wins at sites where a missed night would materially threaten the contract, and the bench is maintained openly rather than secretly, with the incumbent told that every site carries a named alternate as standard practice; at low-consequence sites a best-efforts call list is accepted instead of a paid standby arrangement

edges.why_related: shifting consumables or equipment to the broker lowers the crew's quote but converts a fixed cost into a variable one the residual absorbs, so the apparent saving can be larger than the real one
edges.resolution_rule: compare on total delivered cost rather than on the crew quote alone: whichever split is chosen must be priced into the comparison with a measured consumption assumption and re-tested against actual usage after the first full cycle, and any equipment provision is additionally checked against the verified engagement structure before it is made permanent

edges.why_related: financial remedies are the enforcement mechanism the agreement provides, but applied to a thin-margin crew they can cause the very failure they exist to deter
edges.resolution_rule: fair dealing bounds enforcement: remedies are applied only as the agreement calculates them, only after documented notice and a re-inspection, only prospectively, and only where they were explained before signature; where a remedy would plainly disable the crew from performing, the correct move is condition change, coaching or replacement rather than a deduction that guarantees the next failure

edges.why_related: an accepted quote below the plausible staffing floor is one of the most reliable causes of later crew failure, because the crew closes the gap by cutting hours at the site
ambiguity or omission in the pack shows up downstream as disputed deficiencies and unstable scores, because the crew and the inspector are working from different pictures of the building
a skipped or hurried joint walk produces a cluster of early deficiencies that the corrective ladder then has to absorb, at a cost far above the hour the walk would have taken
verification comes before price is settled, because discovering an entity mismatch or undisclosed onward subcontracting after a number has been agreed forces the whole selection to restart
the independent access path a coverage crew needs is created while credentials are being issued, not on the night the regular crew fails to appear
deficiencies that recur in the same area across different crews indicate a specification defect, which sends the pack back for revision rather than the crew back for correction
the record's history of who performed, who covered and who failed refreshes the supply map's capacity, capability and reliability fields
a deficiency disputed on the ground that the standard never said so is evidence that the standard is underspecified rather than that the crew is uncooperative
the diagnosed causes of failure become screening questions, so the screen learns from every crew that did not work out
both judge whether there is real capacity behind a stated willingness, one crew at a time in the screen and across the whole roster in the portfolio view

conflict_axes.name: supervision_tightness_versus_engagement_structure
conflict_axes.description: Everything that makes quality control stronger - more frequent presence, tighter scheduling, prescriptive instruction, provided equipment - moves the relationship toward the control and integration factors a worker-classification analysis weighs, so the two goals genuinely pull against each other rather than merely appearing to.
poles: supervise tightly to protect the client relationship
preserve the independence pattern the verified structure assumes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: specify observable outcomes and site rules rather than method and manner, keep inspection as verification rather than direction, and treat any genuine need for closer direction as a trigger to re-verify the structure with a qualified professional rather than as a quality decision to make unilaterally

conflict_axes.name: crew_price_pressure_versus_delivery_durability
conflict_axes.description: Every unit of price squeezed out of a crew widens the residual immediately and shortens the life of the arrangement later, because the crew closes the gap with hours at the site rather than with efficiency.
poles: push the crew price as low as it will go
pay a price the crew can still deliver the standard at in month eleven
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: test every quote against the costed labour load rather than against rival quotes alone, decline numbers below the plausible staffing floor, and treat an unavoidably unaffordable site as a bid and margin finding rather than as a negotiating problem

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_staff_versus_vetting_depth
conflict_axes.description: A signed contract carries a start date that the full sequence of screening, reference checking, site visiting, coverage verification and agreement explanation does not always fit inside.
poles: start on the contracted date whatever it takes
complete verification before anyone holds a credential
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: coverage verification and entity confirmation are non-negotiable before a first shift; depth of reference and site verification is scaled to facility consequence; where the sequence genuinely cannot fit, an interim arrangement with a fully verified bench crew is used rather than an unverified permanent one

conflict_axes.name: bench_depth_versus_incumbent_crew_loyalty
conflict_axes.description: Maintaining warm alternates is what makes coverage possible, but a crew that sees the broker courting its rivals reads it as distrust and may reciprocate by deprioritising the site.
poles: keep a deep, actively contacted bench
consolidate around the crews that already perform
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make bench maintenance an openly stated standard practice applied to every site rather than a signal about a particular crew, and size the bench by the consequence of a missed night at each building

conflict_axes.name: prescriptive_scope_versus_method_autonomy
conflict_axes.description: The more precisely the pack tells the crew what to do, the more reliably the building matches the bid - and the closer the instruction comes to directing the manner and method of an independent business's work.
poles: specify everything so nothing is missed
specify outcomes and leave method to the crew
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: write areas, tasks, frequencies, exclusions, safety and site rules exhaustively, and write chemistry, equipment and technique not at all; where a client demands a specific method, carry it as a contractual site rule rather than as the broker's instruction

conflict_axes.name: broker_supplied_versus_crew_supplied_inputs
conflict_axes.description: Supplying consumables and equipment buys consistency and a lower crew quote at the cost of a live variable expense and an additional classification factor; pushing them outward simplifies the month and surrenders control.
poles: control inputs centrally for consistency and price
push inputs to the crew for simplicity and independence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide consumables and equipment separately, compare on total delivered cost with a measured consumption assumption re-tested after the first cycle, and check any equipment provision against the verified structure before making it permanent

conflict_axes.name: inspection_frequency_versus_inspection_cost
conflict_axes.description: Inspection is the only instrument that produces evidence, and it is paid for out of the same residual it protects, so more of it is not automatically better.
poles: walk everything often enough to catch drift early
spend the broker's hours where a failure would cost most
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allocate cadence by consequence with explicit decay and reset rules, vary the hour rather than the count where budget is tight, and treat any site whose spread cannot fund a defensible cadence as a margin question rather than a quality shortcut

conflict_axes.name: coach_the_crew_versus_replace_the_crew
conflict_axes.description: Coaching preserves accumulated building knowledge and a relationship that took months to build; replacing ends a visible failure quickly but resets the learning curve and risks importing the same failure if the cause was never diagnosed.
poles: correct and keep the crew
replace and restart
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: diagnose the cause first and let the cause pick the action: condition causes are fixed rather than coached, execution causes are coached against a defined window with re-inspection, and capability or collapse causes are replaced through the ordered sequence

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_transparency_versus_seamless_single_company_impression
conflict_axes.description: Clients often prefer the feeling of dealing with one integrated company, and every uniform, badge and coverage substitution is an opportunity to let that impression form on its own.
poles: present a seamless single-provider experience
keep the service model explicit at every touchpoint
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: promise accountability loudly and identity never: the broker may say it selects, verifies, inspects and replaces crews and answers at any hour, and may not let a shirt, a signature or a silence imply employment that does not exist

conflict_axes.name: remedy_leverage_versus_fair_dealing_with_a_thin_margin_counterparty
conflict_axes.description: The broker holds the client relationship and the payment timing, which makes enforcement easy and makes overreach invisible until the crew fails or leaves.
poles: enforce remedies firmly to hold the standard
deal fairly with a small business that cannot absorb a shock
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: enforce exactly what was written and explained before signature, prospectively and after documented notice and re-inspection, and where a remedy would disable performance choose condition change, coaching or replacement instead

edge_cases.description: A crew's coverage was verified correctly at signing, but the policy lapses in the middle of the term and nobody notices until an incident occurs at the site
edge_cases.trigger: a renewal date passes without a replacement certificate arriving and no owner was assigned to chase it
edge_cases.mitigation: hold every certificate expiry as a dated field with a named owner and a written suspension consequence, chase before the date rather than after, and pause new shifts rather than continuing on an assumption

edge_cases.description: The engaged crew quietly passes the building to another company, so the people cleaning have never been screened, verified or credentialed by the broker
edge_cases.trigger: the crew takes on more work than it can staff and subcontracts the site onward without telling the broker
edge_cases.mitigation: ask the onward-subcontracting question in the screen and record the answer, address it explicitly in the agreement, verify at inspection that the people present match the crew engaged, and treat an undisclosed pass-through as an immediate escalation rather than a paperwork issue

edge_cases.description: A medical, laboratory or regulated facility imposes background-check, training or access requirements the crew cannot document in time for the contracted start
edge_cases.trigger: the client contract carries facility-specific vetting obligations that the screen did not test for
edge_cases.mitigation: extract the facility's vetting obligation classes from the client contract before screening, make them screening questions, and where they cannot be met in time use a fully verified interim crew rather than starting with undocumented people

edge_cases.description: The client's facility manager begins directing the crew personally on site, adding tasks and adjusting hours without going through the broker
edge_cases.trigger: a helpful crew absorbs on-site requests instead of routing them, and the manager finds it easier to ask the people who are present
edge_cases.mitigation: print the escalation rule in the pack and repeat it at the joint walk, give the crew a scripted redirection to use in the moment, and route every added task back through the broker so it is either priced or declined rather than absorbed

edge_cases.description: A crew quotes a number so far below the others that accepting it would imply fewer hours than the task list can physically be performed in
edge_cases.trigger: a crew wants the work badly, has misread the scope, or intends to staff it thinner than the bid assumed
edge_cases.mitigation: ask the crew to state the hours and headcount behind the number, compare it against the costed labour load, accept only where a documented reason such as existing route density explains it, and otherwise decline rather than accepting a future failure

edge_cases.description: Every person who attended the onboarding walkthrough has left the crew before the first month is out, so nobody on site has ever been calibrated to the standard
edge_cases.trigger: the crew's own staffing churns, which is common in this labour market and invisible to the broker between inspections
edge_cases.mitigation: make personnel change a reportable event in the agreement, reset the inspection cadence to the dense pattern when it occurs, and re-walk the building with the new lead against the same pack version

edge_cases.description: The client offers to engage the crew directly, or the crew approaches the client, so the arrangement the broker built is bypassed
edge_cases.trigger: a satisfied client meets a capable crew and both notice the broker sits between them
edge_cases.mitigation: carry a proportionate non-solicitation term explained before signature, make the broker's continuing contribution visible through inspection evidence and coverage, and treat the approach as a signal about perceived value rather than only as a contractual matter

edge_cases.description: Inspection scores stay comfortably high while the client is plainly unhappy with the building
edge_cases.trigger: inspections always happen at a favourable hour, the inspector has drifted generous, or the instrument does not observe what the occupant actually notices
edge_cases.mitigation: run a calibration inspection with a second inspector at a different hour, compare the client's stated dissatisfaction against the observation list, and add the missing observation to the standard rather than adjusting the score

edge_cases.description: After a crew replacement the credential register does not reconcile: fewer keys or fobs come back than were issued
edge_cases.trigger: credentials were passed informally between crew members over months and never recorded against individuals
edge_cases.mitigation: record issuance at the moment it happens with a named holder, audit before the incoming crew is issued anything, and change the lock or code before the next shift with the client informed rather than hoping the item reappears

edge_cases.description: A single crew holding a large share of the book gives notice, or its business fails, within one notice period
edge_cases.trigger: concentration accumulated quietly because the crew was reliable and every new site was easiest to hand to it
edge_cases.mitigation: track each crew's share of the book against a stated threshold, keep at least one named alternate per site, and stage the transition site by site using the broker-held packs, standards and registers rather than renegotiating everything at once

edge_cases.description: Broker-supplied consumables are being used far faster than the building's occupancy explains
edge_cases.trigger: waste, over-ordering, product used at another site, or a genuine occupancy change nobody told the broker about
edge_cases.mitigation: compare consumption against occupancy on a stated interval, ask the question as a fact-finding conversation before it becomes an accusation, and reset the restock trigger and reporting route if the cause turns out to be a genuine change in the building

edge_cases.description: A crew principal signs an agreement containing remedy and notice terms they cannot comfortably read, and the first enforcement attempt becomes a dispute about what was agreed
edge_cases.trigger: a language or commercial-experience gap that the broker noticed and did not act on
edge_cases.mitigation: walk the enforceable terms through aloud before signature, provide them in the language the principal reads where practical, record that the explanation happened, and offer time to have the agreement reviewed rather than signing on the spot

workflow.action: Restate the signed contract as a delivery mandate before contacting any crew
workflow.description: Fix the building, the bought task list and frequency, the visit pattern, the costed labour load and every cost class the residual must absorb after the crew is paid
workflow.artifact: delivery mandate sheet for the site
workflow.gate: the task list, frequency, visit pattern and costed labour load are stated in the same terms the bid used, and the non-crew cost classes are listed by name

workflow.action: Choose the engagement structure and have the classification question professionally verified
workflow.description: Map the intended operating pattern onto the factor classes, then obtain written verification for the jurisdiction of performance before committing to a structure
workflow.artifact: operating-pattern map and dated professional verification record
workflow.gate: a written verification from a qualified professional exists for the jurisdiction of performance and no classification conclusion has been asserted internally

workflow.action: Refresh the crew supply map for the cluster this building sits in
workflow.description: Confirm which mapped crews already work this geography and these nights, with current capacity headroom, coverage posture and contact recency
workflow.artifact: candidate list drawn from the live supply register
workflow.gate: at least one qualified candidate and one credible alternate exist for the cluster, each contacted within the interval the broker set

workflow.action: Screen candidates against this specific building
workflow.description: Test capacity, personnel, equipment, coverage posture, formation, onward subcontracting and any facility-specific requirement the client contract imposes
workflow.artifact: screening record with a fit or no-fit decision and reason per candidate
workflow.gate: every candidate has a recorded decision with a reason, and the onward-subcontracting answer is documented

workflow.action: Verify the surviving candidates against work they already perform
workflow.description: Run specific reference conversations, visit an existing site at or near working hours where consequence justifies it, and confirm the signing entity matches the trading name and the named insured
workflow.artifact: verification file with reference notes, site observations and entity confirmation
workflow.gate: at least one reference records a specific past failure and its handling, and the entity match is documented

workflow.action: Verify the coverage and bonding obligation classes the contract and jurisdiction require
workflow.description: Obtain certificates from the issuing agent, match named insured to signing entity, confirm policy periods and any required endorsements, and register expiry dates with an owner
workflow.artifact: coverage verification file with tracked expiry dates and suspension rule
workflow.gate: every class the client contract requires is evidenced or listed as an open item, and no shift is scheduled against an unevidenced class

workflow.action: Normalise the scope and take comparable crew quotes
workflow.description: Issue the same task list, frequency calendar, measured areas, supplies split and periodic treatment to each candidate, then test each quote against the costed labour load
workflow.artifact: normalised quote comparison recording implied crew-hours per quote
workflow.gate: all quotes reference the same scope version and any quote below the plausible staffing floor is either explained in writing or declined

workflow.action: Paper the engagement and explain every enforceable term before signature
workflow.description: Settle payment, coverage, supplies and equipment, quality and remedy, subcontracting, non-solicitation, credentials and notice, consistent with the verified structure
workflow.artifact: signed crew agreement with an explanation record
workflow.gate: each term class is present or consciously excluded, the agreement references the pack and standard by version, and the pre-signature explanation is recorded

workflow.action: Build the scope handoff pack and open the credential register
workflow.description: Convert the measured task list into room-by-room task cards, a dated frequency calendar, marked plans, special instructions, exclusions, supply locations and escalation routing, and record every credential at issue
workflow.artifact: versioned site pack plus an opened credential register
workflow.gate: the pack covers every measured area with exclusions stated, carries a version and date, is posted at the site, and every credential issued is recorded against a named holder

workflow.action: Run the joint onboarding walkthrough and stand up coverage before the first billed shift
workflow.description: Walk the building with the crew lead against the pack, fix start time, headcount, lead and nightly completion confirmation, document existing condition at a handover, and confirm the named alternate and independent access path
workflow.artifact: walkthrough record with dated condition photographs and a confirmed coverage arrangement
workflow.gate: the walk is recorded before the first billed shift and a named alternate has received the site summary, agreed emergency terms and an access path that does not run through the regular crew

workflow.action: Publish the inspectable standard and set the risk-weighted cadence
workflow.description: Issue the observable per-task acceptance statements to the crew and schedule the site's inspection frequency from its consequence drivers, with decay and reset rules stated
workflow.artifact: site standard and written inspection cadence with its drivers
workflow.gate: the crew has acknowledged the standard, the cadence names its drivers and reset rule, and the first inspection is scheduled at a varied hour

workflow.action: Score, remedy and record until the transition gate closes
workflow.description: Inspect against the standard with dated evidence, run the corrective ladder on any deficiency, and populate the per-crew and per-site record that the margin and retention side will draw on
workflow.artifact: crew and site record with score trend, deficiencies, closures and coverage events
workflow.gate: the site is not marked transitioned until pack, standard, certificates, credential register, coverage arrangement and first completed inspection all exist in the record

priority_rationale: The frame units come first because every later choice depends on knowing what was actually sold, which engagement structure has been professionally verified, what the client was told about who cleans, which coverage classes must be evidenced, and how crews will be dealt with; sourcing then runs supply map into screen into verification into normalised pricing into a written agreement, because each of those steps is worthless if the one before it was skipped; the handoff units convert the signed scope into a pack, a credential register and a joint walkthrough that calibrate the crew before the first billed shift; the quality units define an inspectable standard, allocate cadence by consequence, score with dated evidence and correct through a written ladder; and the continuity units come last because coverage, failure diagnosis, portfolio exposure and the crew record all compose the earlier work into a system that survives a crew failing and hands measured cost and quality evidence to the margin and retention side of the business.

dominance_rules.rule: Professional verification of the classification question dominates every convenience of supervision, pricing or paperwork
dominance_rules.rationale: misclassification exposure is a back-assessment, penalty and liability class that surfaces long after the operational convenience that caused it has been forgotten
dominance_rules.trigger: any decision that changes direction of work, scheduling, equipment provision, exclusivity or the agreement language
dominance_rules.action: stop, map the change onto the factor classes, and obtain written verification from a qualified professional for the jurisdiction of performance before the change becomes routine

dominance_rules.rule: Truthful disclosure of the service model dominates client comfort, seamlessness and any coverage emergency
dominance_rules.rationale: the business rests on a promise of accountability that is destroyed the moment a client discovers a concealment, and no operational convenience is worth that
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks who employs the cleaners, a coverage crew is deployed, or a shift is missed
dominance_rules.action: state the arrangement plainly, identify a coverage crew as what it is, and report a missed night rather than hoping it passes unnoticed

dominance_rules.rule: Verified coverage classes dominate a contracted start date
dominance_rules.rationale: an uninsured or unbonded crew in a client's building converts an ordinary incident into an unfundable one and breaches the client contract at the same time
dominance_rules.trigger: the start date arrives before certificates, endorsements or entity matching are complete
dominance_rules.action: delay the start or use a fully verified interim crew; never issue credentials or schedule a shift against an unevidenced class

dominance_rules.rule: The written standard dominates a cheaper crew quote
dominance_rules.rationale: a price below the hours the task list physically requires does not buy cheaper delivery, it buys a deferred deficiency, a coverage cost and a client risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a quote implies fewer crew-hours than the costed labour load and the task list can absorb
dominance_rules.action: require the hours and headcount behind the number, accept only with a documented explanation, and otherwise decline and escalate the site as a bid and margin finding

dominance_rules.rule: Site security dominates continuity and cost
dominance_rules.rationale: an unaccounted credential in a commercial building is the one failure that cannot be defended afterwards, whatever it costs to prevent
dominance_rules.trigger: a key, fob, badge or code cannot be accounted for at audit or is reported lost
dominance_rules.action: change the lock or code before the next shift and inform the client, regardless of who bears the cost under the agreement

dominance_rules.rule: The written scope dominates verbal additions made on site
dominance_rules.rationale: absorbed extras destroy the residual invisibly and simultaneously blur who directs the crew's work
dominance_rules.trigger: site staff ask the crew directly for work outside the pack
dominance_rules.action: route the request to the broker to be priced or declined, and have the crew use the scripted redirection rather than absorbing it

dominance_rules.rule: Fair dealing dominates the leverage the broker holds over a crew
dominance_rules.rationale: a crew squeezed or surprised into failure returns as coverage cost, remedy work and client risk, so the ethical rule and the commercial rule point the same way
dominance_rules.trigger: a price negotiation, a remedy application or any moment where a crew's dependence, inexperience or language gap could be used
dominance_rules.action: enforce only what was written and explained before signature, apply remedies prospectively after notice and re-inspection, and never negotiate against an invented competing quote

dominance_rules.rule: Dated evidence dominates impression in every quality decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the record is what a crew is shown at enforcement and what a renewal is argued from, so unevidenced observations weaken both
dominance_rules.trigger: a deficiency, a dispute, or a score that is about to enter the record
dominance_rules.action: record the area, task, date and photograph or leave it out of the record entirely

dominance_rules.rule: Documented capacity dominates a crew's stated willingness
dominance_rules.rationale: willingness is free and headcount is not, and the gap between them is the most common cause of a crew failing in its second month
dominance_rules.trigger: a crew says it can take another building
dominance_rules.action: count the people, the existing sites and the nights already worked, and treat an intention to hire as an intention rather than as capacity

dominance_rules.rule: Coverage readiness dominates residual optimisation at high-consequence sites
dominance_rules.rationale: one visibly missed night at a building that cannot tolerate it costs more than a year of standby readiness
dominance_rules.trigger: a site is being staffed whose missed night would materially threaten the contract
dominance_rules.action: fund a named, pre-briefed alternate with an independent access path before the first shift rather than relying on a call list

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the classification question and choose the engagement structure before quoting or papering any crew
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-verifying, re-papering and renegotiating every crew agreement after the structure turns out to be inconsistent with how the business actually operates

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify coverage classes and entity matching before releasing a pack, a credential or a start date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an uninsured shift that cannot be unwound, and the discovery at incident time that the insured party is not the party that signed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Normalise the scope across candidates before comparing any quote
anti_rework_rules.prevents: choosing a number that was quoted against different work, then re-quoting the whole field once the mismatch surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the supplies and equipment split before the crew prices the building
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mid-term cost argument and a re-priced arrangement after each side discovers the other assumed the opposite

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the inspectable standard before the first inspection rather than after the first dispute
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retroactive standards, disputed deficiencies and a scoring history that cannot be relied on downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the joint onboarding walkthrough before the first billed shift
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a first month consumed by avoidable deficiencies, re-inspections and a client relationship that starts in correction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every credential against a named holder at the moment of issue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unreconcilable audit at crew change and a rekey decision made without knowing what is actually outstanding

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stand up the named alternate and an independent access path before the site goes live
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency sourcing at midnight, a coverage crew locked out of the building, and a client learning about a missed night first

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask and record whether the crew subcontracts any of its work onward before signing anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering unverified, uncredentialed people in a client's building and having to unwind an arrangement already in service

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the deficiency notice, correction window and remedy calculation in the agreement before the first deficiency occurs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad hoc penalties that are disputed, damage the crew relationship, and leave no usable enforcement record

iteration_protocol.trigger: inspection scores at a site trend downward across consecutive visits
iteration_protocol.action: re-inspect against the written standard at a varied hour, run the corrective ladder on what is found, and diagnose whether the cause is execution, condition or specification before escalating

iteration_protocol.trigger: a crew quote arrives materially below what the costed labour load implies the building takes
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the scope normalisation, require the hours and headcount behind the number, and decline or escalate rather than accepting an unsustainable price

iteration_protocol.trigger: a coverage event occurs, whether or not the night was saved
iteration_protocol.action: review detection timing, alternate readiness and the access path, then re-test roster concentration and bench warmth across the affected cluster

iteration_protocol.trigger: the operating pattern with crews changes in any factor-class direction, such as taking over scheduling, providing equipment or requiring exclusivity
iteration_protocol.action: stop, map the change onto the factor classes and obtain fresh written professional verification before the practice becomes routine or is written into agreements

iteration_protocol.trigger: a certificate expiry approaches or passes without a replacement
iteration_protocol.action: chase the issuing agent, suspend scheduling of further shifts under the unevidenced class, and record the gap and its resolution in the crew record

iteration_protocol.trigger: a credential cannot be accounted for or crew personnel with credentials change
iteration_protocol.action: run the credential audit, change the affected lock or code before the next shift, inform the client, and reset the register against named holders

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same area or task fails at multiple sites or under successive crews
iteration_protocol.action: treat the pattern as a specification defect, revise the pack and the standard, reissue both by version, and re-brief the affected crews

iteration_protocol.trigger: a crew principal signals confusion about a term the broker is about to rely on, or disputes that a term was ever explained
iteration_protocol.action: pause enforcement, re-explain in plain language and where practical in the language the principal reads, record the explanation, and only then proceed prospectively

iteration_protocol.trigger: consumable usage at a site diverges from what its occupancy explains
iteration_protocol.action: compare consumption against occupancy over the period, open a fact-finding conversation before any accusation, and reset the restock trigger, reporting route or split if the building genuinely changed
